cbb.player_points_dispersion_by_role.measurement: For each role bucket compute phi = var(points | minutes bucket, expected usage) / mean over the last 3 seasons of player games with weight to the player's own phi_i = n/(n+25) shrinkage; use negative binomial with mean mu and size r = mu/(phi-1) conditional on playing 15+ minutes, mixed with the DNP point mass; output per-rung probabilities; as-of: pregame.
free_sources: Sports-Reference player game logs
Bart Torvik player game stats
raw_data: player points per game with minutes

cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.label: Early-game scoring profile and opening-possession edge for race-to-N markets
cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.mechanism: A race to N points is a first-passage problem: the leader after the opening minutes is determined by the opening lineup's scoring rate, the tip or arrow possession and early turnovers.
cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.rationale: The ledger classifies the only live series (Race to 10, 25, 50) in this archetype, but a first-passage event depends on points per possession in the first 8 to 12 minutes with starters, not on full-game efficiency; race to 50 additionally integrates to about the 28th to 30th minute and is affected by the substitution pattern.
cbb.race_early_scoring_profile.measurement: From play-by-play compute per team the time series of cumulative points in the first 10, 25 and 50 point marks (minutes to reach each), as-of prior games with half-life 12 games; model lambda_A, lambda_B as points per possession of the starters' unit in the first 8 minutes (with shrinkage n/(n+10) to full-game ppp); P(A first to N) from a Skellam-type random walk in possessions with a first-possession edge of about 0.5 possession (tip or arrow, 50 percent) added; as-of: before tip, with lineup status.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play
NCAA live stats archive (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for bulk)
raw_data: play-by-play with clock and score by team

cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.label: Cold-start role and rate prior for transfer and freshman players
cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.mechanism: A player new to a team has no history in the current system; his minutes, usage and per-minute rates must be inferred from previous team production translated through quality and position gaps.
cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.rationale: Because a large share of D1 rotation minutes (a figure to be measured, not assumed) is carried each year by transfers and freshmen new to their team, early-season props for newcomers are priced on prior-team averages even though role and competition change; the translation is non-trivial and is the largest source of early-season error.
cbb.transfer_role_cold_start_prior.measurement: For each newcomer with prior-season D1 stats: prior usage = prev_usage * (prev_team_ORtg_rank / new_team_ORtg_rank)^0.3 shrunk toward the new team's open-minutes distribution by weight depending on departures (minutes available = minutes of lost players / 200); per-minute rate prior = prev rate * conference-strength factor (from the KenPom/Torvik conference ratings gap; the per-tier discount, assumed between 3 and 8 percent, is to be calibrated) + position adjustment; replace with current-season rates as n/(n+10 games). For freshmen use recruiting rank (247 composite) mapped to expected BPM from history. As-of: portal status and roster at the decision time.
free_sources: Sports-Reference previous seasons
247Sports composite and portal tracker (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for bulk export)
Bart Torvik player ratings

cbb.player_stat_covariance.label: Cross-stat covariance of points, rebounds, assists and threes within a player
cbb.player_stat_covariance.mechanism: Stats of the same player are positively correlated through minutes, pace and game state, with a residual correlation after conditioning that depends on role.
cbb.player_stat_covariance.rationale: Combination markets and parlays require the joint probability; independence overstates variance reduction and misprices points-plus-rebounds style thresholds in the tails.
cbb.player_stat_covariance.measurement: Estimate the 4x4 correlation of Pearson residuals of (points, rebounds, assists, threes) given expected minutes by role bucket using the last 3 seasons, shrink each correlation toward the role bucket pooled value with weight n/(n+40); simulate via a Gaussian copula with stat-specific NB marginals conditioned on a shared minutes draw from the minutes mixture; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: Sports-Reference player game logs
Bart Torvik player game stats
raw_data: per-game stat lines with minutes for each player

cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.label: Role-stable effective sample size for shrinkage
cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.mechanism: Games played in a different role (injury return, new starter, teammate absence) carry less information about today's rate than games in the same role.
cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.rationale: Shrinkage constants set by raw game counts under-shrink players whose role changed and over-shrink stable ones; hierarchical estimates need the effective, not nominal, sample.
cbb.role_stable_effective_sample.measurement: n_eff = sum over prior games g of w_g where w_g = exp(-age_g/12 games) * (1 if |minutes_g - expected minutes now| < 6 and starter flag matches else 0.4) * (1 if teammate availability set matches within one starter else 0.7); shrinkage factor k/(n_eff + k) with k = 12 games for rebounds, 20 for points, 30 for threes made; as-of: through prior game.
free_sources: Sports-Reference player logs
ESPN box score starter flags
raw_data: player game log with starter flag and minutes

cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.label: Home-venue scorekeeper bias in recorded assists, blocks and rebounds
cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.mechanism: The official statistician's discretion on assists, steals and blocks varies by venue; the same player's recorded rate differs at home versus away after controlling for his true activity.
cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.rationale: If a home venue systematically credits more assists, an over on assists is cheaper at home than the rate suggests; the effect is stable and cheap to estimate from the difference between home and away rates of visitors.
cbb.venue_scorekeeper_stat_bias.measurement: For each arena compute (assists per 100 team FGM recorded for the home team minus the same teams' away rate) minus league mean home gap, using 3 seasons with shrinkage n/(n+300 team games); likewise blocks per 100 opponent two-point attempts; apply as a multiplicative adjustment capped at +/-6 percent; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED that the effect exists in college data at this size.
free_sources: Sports-Reference team game logs home/away
Bart Torvik game files
raw_data: home and away team assists, blocks, FGM, opponent FGA by game and venue

cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.label: Cause-specific non-appearance probabilities (injury, coach decision, eligibility, suspension)
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.mechanism: Different causes of absence have different base rates, different warning signals and different timing, so a single status probability mixes unlike events.
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.rationale: College players miss games for reasons that never appear in an injury list (coach's decision, academic or eligibility issues, return from injury minutes limits); treating all absences alike loses the signal that a long-listed injury is more informative than a quiet scratch.
cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy.measurement: Classify historical non-appearances of rotation players (top-8 minutes) into causes using news and box score patterns; estimate P(appear) = 1 - sum_c P(cause_c | status label, days since status, program type) with Beta priors by cause (for example injury questionable: 0.55 play; undisclosed: 0.97 play) updated weekly; as-of: status vintage; output also restricted-minutes probability after return (minutes cap 20 in first game back).
free_sources: ESPN injuries and game recaps
team press releases
own captured posts

cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.label: Rebound competition from the other four players on the floor
cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.mechanism: A player's rebounds are his share of a pool, and that share falls with the combined rebound rates of lineup partners on the floor.
cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.rationale: Two good rebounders share one pool; when one is out, the other's rebounds rise by roughly the missing player's share. A per-player rate measured with a different lineup misstates tonight's rate; the effect is largest for bigs.
cbb.rebound_competition_on_floor.measurement: For each lineup scenario k (from availability probabilities), compute share_i,k = r_i / sum_j in lineup(r_j) * team_pool_share, where r is the player's rebound rate per 100 available rebounds estimated from the last 2 seasons with shrinkage n/(n+400 minutes) toward position mean; expected rebounds = sum_k P(k) * minutes_i,k/40 * pool_per_40 * share_i,k; separate for offensive (using team ORB%) and defensive boards; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: Bart Torvik player ORB% and DRB%
Sports-Reference player advanced stats
ESPN play-by-play lineups
raw_data: player ORB% and DRB% by season

cbb.miss_location_mix.label: Expected location mix of missed shots (rim, mid-range, three) and perimeter rebound share
cbb.miss_location_mix.mechanism: Long misses from three-point shots produce longer rebounds that go to guards and wings more often, while rim misses go to bigs; a team's shot mix therefore reallocates the rebound pool among positions.
cbb.miss_location_mix.rationale: A guard's rebound line looks high in games where both teams shoot many threes and low against a rim-oriented opponent; position-blind pool totals miss this reallocation.
cbb.miss_location_mix.measurement: For game g, expected misses by zone M_z = sum over both teams of FGA_z * (1 - make_z) using team shot mix and opponent-adjusted zone make rates; perimeter share of rebounds by position from historical play-by-play: P(guard collects | three-point miss) and P(big collects | rim miss) with shrinkage; player-level adjustment: expected rebounds = sum_z M_z * share_player,z shrunk toward the position mean with n/(n+300). As-of: shot mix over the last 15 games.
free_sources: hoop-math.com team shot zones (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
Sports-Reference shot type splits
ESPN play-by-play shot locations (partial)
raw_data: team shot attempts and makes by zone
rebound events with rebounder and shot type

cbb.assist_conversion_chain.label: Assist chain: potential assists times assisted share of teammates' shots
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.mechanism: Expected assists equal the player's share of team creation times the expected number of team assisted field goals, which depends on the mix of shot types (threes and dunks are mostly assisted, post-ups and isolations rarely).
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.rationale: The assist line moves with the team's expected assisted made baskets, a quantity forecastable from shot mix and shot-quality, not from the player's own assist average; scorer discretion adds a venue term.
cbb.assist_conversion_chain.measurement: expected team assisted FGM = sum_z FGA_z * make_z * assisted_share_z (opponent-adjusted, last 15 games with shrinkage n/(n+10)); player assists = creation_share_i (assists per team assisted FGM while on floor, last 2 seasons, shrunk to role mean with n/(n+600 minutes)) * team assisted FGM * (minutes_i/40) * on-floor adjustment for lineup partners; as-of: prior games and scenario weighting.
free_sources: Sports-Reference team and player assist stats
hoop-math assisted shares (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
raw_data: team assisted and unassisted FGM by shot type

cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.label: Ball-handler succession: who inherits creation when the primary handler is out
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.mechanism: When a primary creator is absent, assists redistribute to the next handler in a team-specific order and a share of creation is lost because the replacement creates less efficiently.
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.rationale: Teammate absence shifts are not symmetric across the roster; some teams have a clear second handler, others spread creation, which changes the sign of the replacement's assist line and the team's total assists.
cbb.ball_handler_succession_map.measurement: From with/without data over the last two seasons, for each team compute the change in assists per 40 for each rotation player when the primary handler (highest assist share) is off the floor, shrinking with n/(n+250 minutes) to a role-mean redistribution (such as 55 percent to the next guard, 25 percent to wings, 20 percent lost); output the redistribution vector; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play for custom with/without
Bart Torvik lineup data (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
raw_data: on/off possession and assist data by player

cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.label: Shared game shooting shock with opposite loadings on rebounds and assists
cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.mechanism: Game-level team shooting luck raises assists and lowers rebounds; the loading depends on role and is the source of the negative dependence between the two stats.
cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.rationale: Combination props and parlays need this dependence; ignoring it overstates the variance of rebounds plus assists for guards and misprices both tails of a combined threshold.
cbb.shooting_shock_loadings.measurement: Estimate a one-factor model on the residuals of rebounds and assists after conditioning on minutes and team pace, with the factor proxy being the standardised team eFG residual in the game; fit loadings lambda_reb and lambda_ast by role (guard, wing, big) over 3 seasons, with shrinkage n/(n+80) to the role pooled loading; simulate stats as NB with means shifted by lambda*z where z ~ N(0,1).
free_sources: Sports-Reference player and team game logs
Bart Torvik game files
raw_data: player rebounds and assists per game

cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.label: Offensive-rebounding crash rate versus transition-defence tradeoff by team
cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.mechanism: Some coaches send multiple players to the offensive glass, which raises offensive rebounds for the crashers and lowers the opponent's defensive-rebound count, while others retreat to prevent transition scoring.
cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.rationale: Offensive rebound totals for a big are partly a scheme choice; a high-crash team facing a low-crash opponent offers more rebounds to every big than their per-minute averages from other matchups.
cbb.crash_vs_get_back_scheme.measurement: For each team compute ORB% (offensive rebounds per available) and opponent transition points per 100 over the last 20 games with half-life 10, shrunk n/(n+10) to the league mean; expected game ORB% for the pair = league mean + 0.5*(crash_A_offense_z + crash_B_defense_allow_z) in standard deviation units of 3.5 points; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: Bart Torvik four factors (ORB%, DRB%)
Sports-Reference team stats
raw_data: team ORB% and DRB% by game

cbb.three_shot_quality_xp.label: Expected make probability per three-point attempt from shot context
cbb.three_shot_quality_xp.mechanism: The make probability depends on shot type (catch-and-shoot versus off the dribble), defender distance, and distance beyond the arc, so expected conversion can be built before looking at the result.
cbb.three_shot_quality_xp.rationale: A shooter on a 44 percent streak from mostly open looks is more likely to regress than the same percentage from contested attempts; the regression target should be quality-implied expectation, not the league mean.
cbb.three_shot_quality_xp.measurement: xP = sum_t share_t * (league_make_t shrunk toward the player's make_t with weight n_t/(n_t + 80)) for shot types t in {assisted catch-and-shoot, unassisted off-dribble, transition, corner vs above-the-break}; blend with skill proxy: xP_final = 0.7*xP + 0.3*(0.35 + 0.30*(FT% - 0.72)) using 2-season FT% with n/(n+120) shrinkage; as-of: through prior game; compare to observed 3P% to define a luck residual and regress it by n_attempts.
free_sources: hoop-math.com three-point splits (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
Sports-Reference assisted shot shares
ESPN play-by-play for assisted flag
raw_data: player three-point attempts and makes by assisted flag and zone
league make rates by shot type

cbb.trailing_three_attempt_lift.label: Three-point attempt lift when trailing and drop when leading
cbb.trailing_three_attempt_lift.mechanism: The attempt rate for threes rises for a team that is behind and falls for a team that leads late, so a shooter's attempts depend on the distribution of game states his team will occupy.
cbb.trailing_three_attempt_lift.rationale: The underdog's shooter has an additional attempts source late in the game that does not exist for the favourite's shooter, and the distribution of attempts therefore depends on the pregame margin distribution, not only on his season average.
cbb.trailing_three_attempt_lift.measurement: From play-by-play estimate for each team the three-point attempt share of FGA as a function of lead (bins -15 to +15) and time remaining (bins of 5 minutes) over the last 2 seasons, shrunk to the league function with weight n/(n+120 possessions); expected attempts = sum over states of P(state | pregame margin distribution) * attempts_per_possession(state) * possessions in state; as-of: prior games; margin distribution from model not market.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play with score and clock
NCAA live stats archive (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
raw_data: play-by-play shot events with score state and clock

cbb.assisted_three_dependency.label: Share of a shooter's threes that are assisted, and by whom
cbb.assisted_three_dependency.mechanism: A spot-up shooter's attempts and quality depend on one or two creators supplying catch-and-shoot passes, so the loss of that creator reduces both attempts and open-look quality.
cbb.assisted_three_dependency.rationale: Assisted share varies from about 40 percent for creators to over 90 percent for stationary shooters; teammate absence shifts for creators raise the shooter's off-dribble attempts at lower quality while shooters' catch-and-shoot attempts fall, so the sign depends on dependence.
cbb.assisted_three_dependency.measurement: For each shooter compute assisted_share = assisted 3PM / total 3PM and assister distribution over the last 2 seasons with shrinkage n/(n+40 makes); with/without effect: delta attempts per 40 and delta make rate when the top assister is off the floor (ridge shrinkage lambda = 150 minutes off); expected scenario shift = sum_k P(creator_k out) * delta_k; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: ESPN play-by-play assist events
Sports-Reference assisted shares

cbb.three_makes_compound_distribution.label: Compound distribution of threes made (minutes, attempts, Beta-uncertain make rate)
cbb.three_makes_compound_distribution.mechanism: Makes are Binomial given attempts and the make probability, attempts are Negative Binomial given minutes, and the make probability has a Beta posterior; marginalising yields the rung probabilities.
cbb.three_makes_compound_distribution.rationale: A plain Poisson on the mean of makes understates the zero and the upper tails because it ignores uncertainty in attempts and in p; rung pricing at 0.5 and 3.5 requires the compound form.
cbb.three_makes_compound_distribution.measurement: For each player-game draw minutes from the minute mixture, attempts ~ NB(mean = rate*minutes*pace factor, dispersion fitted from the last 3 seasons by role, typically var = 1.5*mean), p ~ Beta(a0 + makes_prior, b0 + misses_prior) with an effective prior strength of 100 attempts at xP; makes ~ Binomial(attempts, p); compute P(makes >= k) from 20,000 draws or the analytic Beta-Binomial mixture; as-of: pregame.
free_sources: Sports-Reference player game logs
own model outputs
raw_data: player game logs with 3PA, 3PM and minutes

cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.label: Opponent three-point defence: persistent attempts conceded versus non-persistent percentage allowed
cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.mechanism: A defence's scheme controls the number of threes it concedes, a persistent trait, while the percentage opponents make against it is largely noise.
cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.rationale: Opponent allowed 3P% is routinely used as a matchup input but is mostly luck and should be shrunk almost entirely to the league mean, while the attempt-conceded rate retains most of its signal.
cbb.opp_three_defense_persistence_split.measurement: att_allowed_z = (opponent 3PA allowed per 100 possessions - league mean)/sd, last 15 games half-life 8 with shrinkage n/(n+10) to prior season value; pct_allowed_z = (opponent 3P% allowed - league)/sd shrunk by weight 0.1 only (set from persistence tests); matchup adjustment to shooter's attempts = 0.6 * att_allowed_z * team-level sd of attempts effect (about 0.8 attempts) and to p = 0.1 * pct_allowed_z * 1.5 points; as-of: prior games.
free_sources: Bart Torvik team three-point rate and percentage allowed
Sports-Reference team defence stats

cbb.strength_evolution_to_march.label: Distribution of team strength change from pricing date to Selection Sunday
cbb.strength_evolution_to_march.mechanism: Team strength evolves through development, rotation settling, transfer integration and injuries; the change from a given date to March is a random variable with a team-type-dependent sd.
cbb.strength_evolution_to_march.rationale: A November title probability is an expectation over March strength; using today's rating as if it were March's understates tail teams and overstates favourites, and the correct sd depends on roster continuity and age.
cbb.strength_evolution_to_march.measurement: For each past season and each date d (weekly), compute delta = rating_March (final pre-tournament adjusted margin) - rating_d for each team; regress delta on rating_d (mean reversion), games_played_d, returning minutes share, roster age (minutes-weighted class year), and injury indicator; model delta ~ N(b*(rating_d - league_mean), sd_d) with sd_d = sqrt(a^2 + c^2*(games_remaining/30)) fitted on at least 12 seasons; output the posterior over March rating by team; as-of: rating snapshot date.
free_sources: Bart Torvik time machine
Sports-Reference historical team ratings (SRS)
own daily rating snapshots
raw_data: team rating by date for each season

cbb.pod_site_proximity.label: Distance from campus to first- and second-round site and expected crowd imbalance
cbb.pod_site_proximity.mechanism: The NCAA places pods across the country and seeds are matched to sites by geography, so some teams play 50 miles from home and others 2,000, with corresponding crowd and travel effects.
cbb.pod_site_proximity.rationale: A near-home team in rounds 1 and 2 gets a semi-home margin bonus of one to three points relative to a neutral model, and a distant 2-seed may be at a relative disadvantage; the effect compounds through two rounds of the path.
cbb.pod_site_proximity.measurement: For each team-seed-site combination compute great-circle distance campus to arena in miles, a binary indicator for within 250 miles, and an attendance-share proxy (school's average road attendance rank); margin adjustment = b1*I(<250 mi) + b2*log(distance) fitted on 20 tournaments of game margins vs rating-implied margins (expected b1 about 1.5 to 2.5 points, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); applied only to rounds 1 and 2 (and regional sites if close); as-of: bracket release.
free_sources: NCAA.com site assignments
Sports-Reference tournament game results with sites

cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.label: Conference tournament format table for 2026-27 (size, byes, hosting, seeding, tiebreakers)
cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.mechanism: Each league has its own bracket: number of participants, byes for top seeds, campus versus neutral venue, reseeding, tiebreakers that set seeds, and days of rest between games.
cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.rationale: More than thirty ledger series settle on a conference tournament; probability for the top seed varies by format as much as by rating (a top seed with a double bye needs three wins in a 14-team field, a four-team Ivy field needs two), and some formats let the higher seed host.
cbb.conf_tournament_format_table.measurement: Maintain a table with fields: league, teams in field, rounds, byes by seed, hosting rule (neutral, campus, higher-seed), venue city, dates, tiebreaker order for regular-season seeding, auto-bid flag; simulate the league bracket from the current standings projection using the model's pairwise win probability with a home adjustment of 3.5 points where the format hosts; refresh when conferences announce changes (realignment, new members) before each season; as-of: announcement date.
free_sources: Conference websites and NCAA.com
Wikipedia conference tournament pages (cross-check)

cbb.two_way_balance_profile.label: Two-way balance profile: joint offence and defence rank at the top of the rating list
cbb.two_way_balance_profile.mechanism: Champions in the efficiency era have mostly been ranked highly in both offence and defence; a team strong on only one side may have a different tournament win probability than its net rating suggests because of matchup variance.
cbb.two_way_balance_profile.rationale: This is a hypothesis from historical regularities, not an established causal driver; it is included as a testable signal because it could capture shot-making variance in single games (offence-dependent teams have wider outcomes).
cbb.two_way_balance_profile.measurement: Compute min(off_rank, def_rank) and the absolute difference |off_rank - def_rank| in the final pre-tournament snapshot; flag balanced if both top 25 or the minimum rank 20 or better; test in historical tournaments whether the residual of advancement versus rating-implied probability (probit) is explained by the balance flag after controlling for net rating (a likelihood-ratio test across at least 20 tournaments); as-of: Selection Sunday snapshot.
free_sources: Bart Torvik historical ratings
Sports-Reference historical team ratings
raw_data: pre-tournament offence and defence ranks by team per season

cbb.tournament_field_format.label: NCAA tournament field structure and seeding rules for 2027
cbb.tournament_field_format.mechanism: The number of teams, play-in games, at-large and automatic bids, seeding S-curve and region placement rules define which paths exist and how many rounds each team must win.
cbb.tournament_field_format.rationale: The sampled round series refers to a 'Round of 76', which implies a field larger than the 68-team format; this changes bubble probabilities, the number of games for the lowest seeds and the title path for play-in teams, so any title model built on the 68-team structure may be wrong.
cbb.tournament_field_format.measurement: Record for the season: field size, number of first-round or play-in games, number of automatic and at-large bids, rounds required for each seed line, S-curve rules, bracket-integrity rules (conference avoidance until a specified round) and effective dates; simulate seed to path accordingly; as-of: NCAA announcement date; verify against NCAA.com before each season.
free_sources: NCAA.com announcements
NCAA tournament selection principles PDF
raw_data: field size and bid counts by season

cbb.committee_ordinal_seed_model.label: Committee ordinal seed-line model from resume metrics and fundamentals ratings (no bracketology consensus)
cbb.committee_ordinal_seed_model.mechanism: The selection committee assigns seed lines by ranking teams on results-based team-sheet metrics and consulted predictive ratings; an ordered model fitted to past committee outputs reproduces that ranking without using any outside forecast of it.
cbb.committee_ordinal_seed_model.rationale: The catalog input cbb.committee_seed_model blends an ordinal model with the Bracket Matrix consensus, which is an expert forecast and therefore a benchmark. Seed and field-membership contracts need the market-free and expert-free model so its edge over consensus can be measured.
cbb.committee_ordinal_seed_model.measurement: Ordered logit (cutpoints for seed lines 1 to 16 plus 'not in field') of final seed on NET rank, Quad 1 wins, Quad 3 and Quad 4 losses, WAB, SOR, last-10 record, conference-champion indicator and AdjEM_fund (cbb.ratings_fundamentals), fitted on Selection Sunday team sheets from 2018-19 (the first NET season) through the latest season, excluding the cancelled 2020 tournament, with leave-one-season-out validation and a protocol-vintage indicator for rule changes; to project before Selection Sunday, simulate remaining regular-season and conference-tournament games with the ratings model and re-evaluate the metrics per simulation; no Bracket Matrix or sportsbook input.
free_sources: NCAA NET rankings and team sheets (ncaa.com; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for scrape access and history)
Warren Nolan (warrennolan.com) NET, quadrant records and SOS (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for archived sheets)
Barttorvik WAB (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for history)
raw_data: Selection Sunday team sheets by team and season (NET, quadrant records, WAB, SOR)
final seed lines and field membership by season

cbb.top_n_tie_inclusive_cutoff.label: Tie-inclusive top-N cutoff probability from the joint conference win-total distribution
cbb.top_n_tie_inclusive_cutoff.mechanism: A team finishes in the top N if its conference wins are at least the N-th highest total among all teams, with every tied team counting.
cbb.top_n_tie_inclusive_cutoff.rationale: Standings simulations that apply conference tiebreakers produce a rank, but the contract ignores tiebreakers and pays all tied teams; using tiebreaker ranks understates probabilities near the cutoff and makes team probabilities sum to exactly N when the contract's sum exceeds N.
cbb.top_n_tie_inclusive_cutoff.measurement: Simulate the conference season 20,000 times: draw each team's strength from its posterior, draw every remaining conference game with home-adjusted probit probability, tally conference wins; for each simulation compute W_N = N-th largest win total; team i hits if W_i >= W_N; probability = hit frequency; report the expected number of teams hitting (greater than N); as-of: standings and ratings snapshot with remaining games.
free_sources: Conference standings and schedules (ESPN, Sports-Reference)
own simulation from ratings

cbb.strength_uncertainty_game_correlatio.label: Shared-strength correlation among a team's game outcomes
cbb.strength_uncertainty_game_correlatio.mechanism: Because one latent strength governs all of a team's games, outcomes are positively correlated; the Poisson-binomial with independent games understates tails.
cbb.strength_uncertainty_game_correlatio.rationale: Undefeated and 30-win series sit in the extreme upper tail, where integrating over strength uncertainty increases the probability by large factors relative to plugging in the mean; the same shared factor raises the variance of every win total.
cbb.strength_uncertainty_game_correlatio.measurement: Draw s_i ~ N(rating_i, sd_t) with sd_t = sqrt(a^2 + b*(games_remaining/30)) calibrated so that the realised distribution of final win totals matches history (a ~ 1.5 points, b ~ 4 for new rosters); condition each game's probability on s_i and s_j; compute P(all wins) = E_s[prod_g p_g(s)] by Monte Carlo (20,000 draws); calibrate sd_t on 15 prior seasons by checking coverage of final win totals (probability integral transform uniformity); as-of: rating snapshot.
free_sources: Bart Torvik / Sports-Reference historical ratings and results
own simulation
raw_data: historical preseason and in-season ratings with final records

cbb.regular_season_game_inventory.label: Regular-season game inventory: number of games, sites, opponent class and which count as official
cbb.regular_season_game_inventory.mechanism: The event space for win totals, undefeated and home-only series is the list of games that count, which depends on exempt events, non-D1 opponents, neutral sites and the league's definition.
cbb.regular_season_game_inventory.rationale: A 30-win strike on a team that plays 29 counted games is impossible, and one that plays 31 allows a loss; the home-only series has between 14 and 17 games and excludes all neutral-site games; each ambiguity changes the probability by a large factor.
cbb.regular_season_game_inventory.measurement: Per team and season record: scheduled games (date, opponent, site type home/away/neutral, event name, D1 flag, counts toward official record flag, conference flag) from the school and NCAA schedule; total counted games N, home counted games H; probability tables computed over counted games only; refresh when the schedule changes (cancellations, added games); as-of: schedule snapshot date.
free_sources: Sports-Reference schedule pages
NCAA stats site schedules
School athletic sites
raw_data: team schedules with site type and event labels

cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.label: Dependence of two teams' tournament advancement (region, pod, avoidance rules)
cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.mechanism: Two teams' advancement probabilities are linked through the bracket: they cannot both advance if they meet, and share region and pod strength.
cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.rationale: KXNCAAMBBOTHQUAL asks for both teams in the Round of 16; the committee generally avoids same-conference matchups before the third round for teams of the same conference, but region and pod placement still matter and a correlation from correlated rating uncertainty exists.
cbb.joint_advancement_dependence.measurement: Simulate the bracket 50,000 times from the seed and region distribution (before Selection Sunday) or from the actual bracket (after): P(both reach R16) = joint frequency; also report the independence benchmark P_A*P_B and the ratio; the committee rule used is: same-conference teams avoided in rounds 1 and 2 where possible (verify yearly with the NCAA's principles and procedures document); as-of: bracket release.
free_sources: NCAA.com bracket
NCAA selection principles document
Bracket Matrix for pre-bracket projections

cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.label: Effort and rotation change after clinching or elimination from title races
cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.mechanism: Teams that have clinched a seed or title, or are out of any race, may rest starters or alter intensity in the last games, which shifts win probabilities against the pure strength gap.
cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.rationale: Top-N and win-total contracts include the last two weeks of the conference season in which stakes differ across teams; an incentive-blind model overstates the win probability of clinched teams and understates that of teams chasing a bid or a top-four double bye.
cbb.clinch_and_elimination_effort_shift.measurement: Define stakes_i,g = |dP(top4 finish)/d(win this game)| from the standings simulation and the bubble/seed leverage from the resume model; regress game margin residuals (actual minus rating-implied) on stakes_i - stakes_j and a clinch flag using 8 seasons of the final 6 conference games; expected effect 0.5 to 1.5 points (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); as-of: standings before each game.
free_sources: Sports-Reference game results
own standings simulation
raw_data: seed and bid leverage computed by simulation

cbb.remaining_game_resume_leverage.label: Resume leverage of each remaining game (win and loss value by opponent quadrant and site)
cbb.remaining_game_resume_leverage.mechanism: Each remaining game moves NET, quadrant records, WAB and SOR by amounts that depend on the opponent's rank and the site, so the final resume is a function of which games remain and who the team beats.
cbb.remaining_game_resume_leverage.rationale: A bubble team's field probability depends more on whether its remaining games are Q1 opportunities (large upside, small downside) or Q4 traps (small upside, large downside) than on the average strength of remaining opponents.
cbb.remaining_game_resume_leverage.measurement: For each remaining game g compute dWAB_win_g and dWAB_loss_g from the WAB formula using current opponent ranks and site; leverage_g = P(win_g) * dWAB_win + (1 - P(win_g)) * dWAB_loss; also compute dNET rank change by Monte Carlo (NET approximated by team value index and efficiency); aggregate final resume distribution by simulating all remaining games including conference tournament; as-of: current resume snapshot and schedule; recompute daily.
free_sources: NCAA NET rankings and team sheets (NCAA.com)
WarrenNolan team sheets
ESPN resume pages
Bart Torvik WAB tables
raw_data: opponent NET ranks and sites for remaining games

cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.label: Revealed committee weights on NET, WAB, SOR, quadrant record and predictive ratings by seed range
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.mechanism: The committee's ranking behaves like a latent score over the metrics with weights that differ at the top of the field and on the bubble.
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.rationale: Using KenPom or NET alone ranks teams as an analyst would, not as the committee did; an ordered-probit fit on past seeds reveals that, for instance, quality wins count more at the top and bad losses more on the bubble.
cbb.committee_metric_revealed_weights.measurement: For seasons 2018 to 2026 (post-NET) fit an ordered probit for final seed (1 to 16, plus missed) on standardised NET rank, WAB, SOR, KPI, KenPom rank, Q1 wins, Q3+Q4 losses and conference tournament result, with weights allowed to vary in three seed bands (1-4, 5-10, 11-16 and bubble) via interaction terms; regularise with ridge; output coefficient vector with standard errors and the committee noise sd; as-of: metrics at Selection Sunday and weekly in March.
free_sources: NCAA.com NET archive and team sheets
Bart Torvik/KenPom archives
Sports-Reference bracket history
Bracket Matrix archive
raw_data: final seeds and field per year
metric values at Selection Sunday per team per year

cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.label: Committee protocol vintage: metrics used, quadrant definitions, field size and bracketing rules
cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.mechanism: The metrics on the team sheet, the quadrant thresholds, the number of bids and the bracketing rules change from year to year, shifting the relevant weights.
cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.rationale: Quadrant definitions and metric lists have been revised (for example the addition of WAB, adjustments to quadrant thresholds) and the field size may change for 2027 (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); a model fit on earlier years can be mis-specified for the current protocol.
cbb.committee_protocol_vintage.measurement: Maintain a per-season record: metrics on team sheet, quadrant thresholds for home, neutral and away games, number of at-large and automatic bids, play-in structure, bracketing principle changes; indicator variables for protocol changes and a protocol-vintage weight for each historical season (1.0 for current protocol, 0.5 for one prior change, 0.25 for earlier) used in the fits; as-of: NCAA announcement dates.
free_sources: NCAA.com committee principles and procedures
NCAA news releases

cbb.recency_weighting_in_seeding.label: Committee weighting of recent results relative to the full season
cbb.recency_weighting_in_seeding.mechanism: Committee members may weigh the last month of results and the conference tournament more heavily than early-season results, in contrast to metrics that weigh the season equally.
cbb.recency_weighting_in_seeding.rationale: If recency is rewarded, late-season rises and falls move seed lines beyond what the cumulative metrics show; estimating it prevents using a static season-long metric when late results matter.
cbb.recency_weighting_in_seeding.measurement: From the ordered-probit residuals (actual seed minus metric-implied seed) regress on last-10-games win share relative to season win share, last-10 efficiency margin minus season efficiency margin, and conference tournament games won, using 8 seasons; as-of: Selection Sunday; report coefficient with standard errors; use a prior of zero with a ridge shrinkage that corresponds to an sd of 0.5 seed lines per standard deviation of the recency variable.
free_sources: Sports-Reference game logs
NCAA.com seeds archive

cbb.committee_availability_treatment.label: Seed adjustment for key players missing at Selection Sunday
cbb.committee_availability_treatment.mechanism: The committee takes player availability into account in some way, so a team missing a star may be placed lower (or protected) than metrics alone imply.
cbb.committee_availability_treatment.rationale: An injury late in the season changes how good the team is without changing its resume; whether the committee seeds on full-strength or current-strength is a discrete, partially discretionary choice with a few lines at stake.
cbb.committee_availability_treatment.measurement: From past years list teams with a rotation player (top 3 by minutes or BPM) out at Selection Sunday, compute seed residual from the revealed-preference model, estimate the mean residual by player importance (BPM share) with a prior mean of -0.5 lines and a sd of 1.0, shrinking by n/(n+10); as-of: injury status published before Selection Sunday.
free_sources: News archives and team statements
Sports-Reference rosters
raw_data: injury list at Selection Sunday per team per year

cbb.number_one_transition_model.label: Markov model of the #1 holder and successor distribution after a loss
cbb.number_one_transition_model.mechanism: The distinct-#1 count is 1 plus the number of changes at the top in which the new holder has not been #1 before; changes occur when the current #1 loses (or is leapfrogged) and the successor is drawn from the contenders.
cbb.number_one_transition_model.rationale: A threshold such as 9 distinct #1 teams is far into the tail of a process whose typical value is 3 to 6 (to be computed from AP archives, not asserted), so the tail depends on the weekly leapfrog probability and on how often the successor is a new team; neither is a function of ratings alone.
cbb.number_one_transition_model.measurement: State: current #1, set of previous #1s, week t (1 to 19). Transition: P(change in week t) = 1 - (1 - L_t) where L_t = prob #1 loses in the week plus P(leapfrog without a loss) estimated from AP archives 2000 to 2026 (leapfrog rate about 3 to 8 percent per week, to be fitted); successor chosen by softmax over the top-8 contenders with features (poll points gap, record, rating gap, unbeaten flag) fitted on past changes; count distinct holders via Monte Carlo of 20,000 seasons using game-by-game loss probabilities from the ratings of the top teams; as-of: latest poll and schedule.
free_sources: AP poll archive (apnews.com / Sports-Reference AP poll history)
ESPN poll archive
own ratings
raw_data: weekly AP poll top 8 with points

cbb.ap_voter_ballot_panel.label: AP voter ballot panel: individual ballots and update rules
cbb.ap_voter_ballot_panel.mechanism: The AP poll aggregates individual ballots published by voter; each voter's update after results has its own inertia and preferences, so the aggregate response to a loss is the sum of heterogeneous responses.
cbb.ap_voter_ballot_panel.rationale: A voter-level model captures both the average reaction to a loss and the dispersion that makes top-two ties or leapfrogs likely; aggregate-only models cannot tell whether a swing is a few extreme voters or broad movement.
cbb.ap_voter_ballot_panel.measurement: Collect each weekly ballot (voter id, ranks 1 to 25); for each voter-team-week compute rank change as a function of the team's result (win/loss, opponent rank, margin, site), prior rank and a voter fixed effect; fit a mixed model with voter random slopes using 5 seasons; simulate the poll as the sum of voter points from the fitted update rules (25 points for 1st down to 1 for 25th); as-of: previous poll plus results.
free_sources: AP Top 25 voter ballots published on apnews.com (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for archive depth and bulk access)

cbb.final_ap_rank_mapping.label: Mapping from tournament outcome and pre-tournament rank to final AP rank
cbb.final_ap_rank_mapping.mechanism: The Final poll orders teams by tournament success first and pre-tournament rank second, with the champion typically placed first or near first.
cbb.final_ap_rank_mapping.rationale: A final-rank contract equals the probability of a bracket outcome mapped through the ordering rule; without the mapping, a top 10 contract would be priced as a rank persistence question, which is wrong because many pre-tournament top-10 teams lose early and fall out.
cbb.final_ap_rank_mapping.measurement: From 2000 to 2026 regress final AP rank on round reached (champion, runner-up, Final Four, Elite Eight, Sweet 16, earlier, missed tournament), pre-tournament AP rank, seed and margin of last game with an ordinal model; output P(final rank = k | round reached, pre rank) with noise sd about 1.5 places; combine with bracket_sim round-reached probabilities by Monte Carlo; as-of: bracket release, updated per round.
free_sources: Sports-Reference AP final polls and tournament results
ESPN AP poll history

cbb.kenpom_rank_projection.label: Replication and projection of KenPom ratings to a timestamp
cbb.kenpom_rank_projection.mechanism: KenPom's rating is an opponent-adjusted efficiency margin computed from all completed games with venue and recency treatment, so the rank at a future time is a function of the results that will be counted before that time.
cbb.kenpom_rank_projection.rationale: KXNCAAMBKENPOMRANK and KXNCAAMBKENPOMTOP settle on a snapshot list; the uncertainty is the future results and the rating algorithm, not human opinion, so a faithful replication (with game-by-game updates) is the only way to evaluate crowded ranks.
cbb.kenpom_rank_projection.measurement: Compute AdjO, AdjD and tempo by iterating opponent adjustment to convergence on all D1 games with venue factor 1.4 percent per side (approximate) and a decay weighting by game recency, calibrated so replicated AdjEM matches the KenPom value on historical snapshots with RMSE below 0.3 points; project to Mar 15 12:00 by simulating each remaining game (including conference tournaments) with the pairwise win and margin model, re-running the adjustment per simulated day, and recording rank distributions; as-of: simulation start date, cutoff time of the timestamp.
free_sources: Bart Torvik T-Rank (similar algorithm, free)
KenPom (paid) for calibration
Sports-Reference game results
raw_data: all D1 game results with venue
remaining schedule with conference tournament brackets

cbb.award_selection_model.label: Award selection model: candidate sets, team success dependence and co-recipient probability
cbb.award_selection_model.mechanism: Award winners come from a candidate set defined by performance and team success; the Most Outstanding Player depends on the champion, while Player of the Year awards weigh production, team rank and narrative.
cbb.award_selection_model.rationale: Three contract families (tournament MOP, national player of the year, conference awards) have different drivers; treating them all as 'production' misses that MOP is mostly a title contract, and a 1/N split changes the expected payout.
cbb.award_selection_model.measurement: For MOP: P(player) = sum over teams of P(team champion) * share_player|champion, where share is a multinomial logit on Final Four box-score points per game and star flags fitted to 1990 to 2026 MOP history (champion-conditioned) plus a 3 to 6 percent chance MOP comes from a non-champion; for POY and conference awards: multinomial logit among candidates on BPM, points per game, team rank and conference record, with year-specific fixed effects; co-recipient rate from history (about 1 to 3 percent for major awards); expected payout = P(win) * E[1/N]; as-of: vote deadline and latest stats.
free_sources: Sports-Reference award histories
Wikipedia award winner lists
NCAA tournament MOP records
raw_data: player season statistics and team rank at vote time

cbb.stat_leader_race_model.label: Leaderboard race model for per-game statistic leaders with postseason games and thresholds
cbb.stat_leader_race_model.mechanism: The leader is the maximum of many noisy per-game averages; future games (including postseason) add samples, injuries remove candidates and thresholds filter qualifiers.
cbb.stat_leader_race_model.rationale: Current leaders are biased upward by luck, so naive extrapolation overstates their chance; the probability that a given player ends first depends on current gap, remaining games (about 8 to 12 for a team after the point of pricing), per-game sd and the probability of missing games.
cbb.stat_leader_race_model.measurement: For each candidate (top 30 by current average, qualified or near-qualified): posterior of true per-game mean mu_i with shrinkage n/(n+15 games) toward a role prior; per-game sd s_i from game logs; remaining games G_i = scheduled regular season games + P(conference tournament games) + expected NCAA, NIT, Crown, CBI and CIT games from bracket_sim (all official games count, including non-conference ones); availability probability a_i per game; simulate final average = (sum so far + sum future)/(games played) for 20,000 seasons applying the NCAA minimum threshold rule for qualification; P(leader) = frequency of max; as-of: stats through prior game.
free_sources: NCAA stats leaderboards (stats.ncaa.org)
Sports-Reference player season and game logs
raw_data: current per-game averages and game logs

cbb.poll_calendar_and_protocol.label: AP poll calendar and designation rules (number of polls, Preseason and Final labels, release timing)
cbb.poll_calendar_and_protocol.mechanism: The number of opportunities for a change at #1 or for a team to enter the top 5 equals the number of polls, and which poll counts as 'Final' is the AP's designation.
cbb.poll_calendar_and_protocol.rationale: Settlement rules count every poll including Preseason and Final and rely on the AP's own labels; a missed week, an early holiday poll or a shifted Final release date changes the count and the resolution timing.
cbb.poll_calendar_and_protocol.measurement: Maintain per season: dates of Preseason, each weekly poll, and Final; number of polls N_polls; AP's 'expected release' date for the Final poll (Apr 6, 2027 expected); poll week labels; indicator for the year-specific schedule; used as the horizon in the transition model and the any-week model; as-of: AP schedule publication.
free_sources: AP Top 25 pages (apnews.com)
ESPN poll pages
raw_data: poll release dates and labels by season

cbb.award_candidate_profile.label: Award candidate profile: production, team success and voter-criteria features by award type
cbb.award_candidate_profile.mechanism: Award voters (national media panels, conference coaches or media) pick from candidates by scoring and overall production, team success, role-specific criteria (defence for Defensive Player of the Year, class for freshman honours) and narrative; a per-award choice model on those features gives the winner distribution.
cbb.award_candidate_profile.rationale: The record's award stage had only cbb.news and a usage rate, which cannot separate candidates for conference awards such as Defensive Player of the Year or Newcomer awards whose criteria differ from player of the year. Voter bodies and criteria differ by award, so one pooled model is wrong.
cbb.award_candidate_profile.measurement: For each award type separately, fit a conditional (multinomial) logit across candidates within each past award-season: features are team AdjEM_fund rank and win percentage, player BPM or Torvik PRPG rank, points, rebounds, assists, steals plus blocks per game, defensive rating or block/steal rates (Defensive Player of the Year only), class (freshman or newcomer indicator for those awards), previous all-conference selection, preseason watch-list membership; train on all available seasons per award (at least 10 where history exists, otherwise pool with an award-type indicator), as-of the last games before voting closes; output candidate shares, then split payout probability for ties (1/N rule).
free_sources: Sports-Reference award and all-conference pages (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for voting totals)
conference websites for award announcements
Bart Torvik player tables (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for history)
raw_data: award winners and finalists by award and season
player season statistics and advanced ratings
team results and ratings at voting close

cbb.d3_team_rating.label: Division III team rating (margin-based, opponent- and venue-adjusted)
cbb.d3_team_rating.mechanism: A Division III game margin is generated by the same possession process as a D1 game, but neither team appears in D1 rating systems, so the strength gap must come from a rating fitted on the D3 schedule graph.
cbb.d3_team_rating.rationale: KXNCAAMBD3GAME lists D3 games (the sampled market is the DIII national final). D1 ratings, tier priors and the D1 home-court constant do not apply; D3 rosters change each year with no portal-scale data, and late-season D3 tournament games are often at campus sites, so venue must be modelled explicitly. Without this input the archetype has no strength term for a whole series.
cbb.d3_team_rating.measurement: Ridge-regressed least-squares margin rating on all D3-vs-D3 games of the current season up to the as-of time: margin_ij = r_i - r_j + h*home_ij + e, home term h fitted per season (prior 3.0 pts, sd 1.5), game weight exp(-days/60), ridge penalty equivalent to 8 games at the prior mean. Prior mean r_i = 0.55 * last season's final rating, reverted to conference mean. Margins capped at 25 to limit blowout leverage. Win probability = Phi(gap / 11). Units: points per game; snapshot stored daily with as-of timestamp, using only games final before pricing.
free_sources: stats.ncaa.org Division III scoreboards and box scores (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED scrape terms)
d3hoops.com scoreboards (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
Massey Ratings Division III ratings page (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED history)
raw_data: D3 game results: date, home team, away team, neutral flag, final score

cbb.round_max_team_score.label: Distribution of the highest team score in a tournament round, with tie mass
cbb.round_max_team_score.mechanism: The most-points contract settles on the maximum of all team scores in a round, which depends on every game's joint score distribution and on which teams are playing.
cbb.round_max_team_score.rationale: A team's chance of the round maximum is not its chance of a high team total: it depends on how many other teams play, their tempo and efficiency, and the overtime chance of each game. Ties at the maximum split the payout 1/N, so the integer tie mass must be modelled. Before the round's participants are known, advancement uncertainty multiplies in.
cbb.round_max_team_score.measurement: For the named round, take the participating games from the bracket at the as-of time; for rounds not yet set, draw participants from cbb.bracket_sim. For each game draw (team A pts, team B pts) jointly from the team-total model (tempo, adjusted offence/defence, cbb.team_points_margin_coupling, OT mixture from cbb.ot_period_tie_chain, i.e. P(tie at end of regulation) from the model margin distribution, never a spread-bucketed rate), add a shared round-level scoring shock N(0, 2 pts). Over 100,000 simulations compute, per team, E[payout] = sum over sims of 1{team score = max} / N_tied, truncated down to the cent. As-of: ratings and bracket frozen at pricing time.
free_sources: NCAA bracket and schedule pages (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED archive)
Sports-Reference tournament box scores (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED terms)
raw_data: tournament bracket with round composition and game times
per-team adjusted offence, defence and tempo as of pricing
historical tournament team scores by round for calibration of the round-level shock

cbb.secondary_postseason_field_model.label: Selection into the NIT and College Basketball Crown fields for teams left out of the NCAA tournament
cbb.secondary_postseason_field_model.mechanism: A team can win the NIT or the Crown only if it is not in the NCAA field, is eligible under that event's conference allocation and accepts the invitation, so the field is a filtered set of bubble and near-bubble teams.
cbb.secondary_postseason_field_model.rationale: Title probability for these events is non-monotone in team strength: strong teams are removed by NCAA selection, conference-allocated slots (Crown slots tied to specific leagues, NIT slots for others) decide who is eligible, and opt-outs by teams that decline are common. Pricing them with the NCAA bracket logic or with strength alone gives the strongest teams large probabilities that are in fact near zero.
cbb.secondary_postseason_field_model.measurement: P(field_e | team) = P(not in NCAA field) from cbb.committee_ordinal_seed_model, times P(eligible for event e) from a per-season table of that event's slot rules (conference allocations, NET-rank cut-offs, at-large slots) applied to the simulated end-of-season NET rank, times an acceptance rate estimated from past invitation and decline lists (shrunk to the event mean with weight n/(n+20)); field composition is simulated jointly with the NCAA selection draw, then the event bracket is simulated with cbb.ratings_fundamentals at neutral or host sites. As-of: rule table versioned by announcement date; all ranks as of the pricing time.
free_sources: NIT and Crown official field announcements and bracket pages (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for archived slot rules)
NCAA NET archive (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED depth)
raw_data: per-season NIT and Crown slot rules and conference allocations
past NIT/Crown fields, seeds and declined invitations
end-of-season NET ranks of non-NCAA teams

cbb.wcbb_title_probability.label: Women's Division I national title probability by team (for men's-and-women's combo contracts)
cbb.wcbb_title_probability.mechanism: The women's champion is decided by a separate 68-team bracket; a combo contract pays only if the named women's team also wins, so the women's marginal is a required factor.
cbb.wcbb_title_probability.rationale: KXNCAAMB2ML conjoins a men's and a women's champion. The women's game has more concentrated strength (a few dominant programmes, fewer upsets), top seeds host first and second rounds, and its ratings and injury news are separate; none of the men's inputs provide this factor, and the two tournaments share no games, so the joint is approximately the product.
cbb.wcbb_title_probability.measurement: Simulate the women's bracket 100,000 times from an opponent-adjusted women's efficiency rating (points per 100 possessions, game weight exp(-days/45), ridge prior from last season's final rating x 0.6) with a game sd of 11 points, home court of 3 points for campus-hosted early rounds; before Selection Sunday draw the field and seeds from an ordered-probit on women's NET and resume. Output P(champion) per team as of pricing time; combo price = P_men x P_women, with a sensitivity check on correlation 0.
free_sources: Her Hoop Stats (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED free tier fields)
NCAA women's NET and stats.ncaa.org (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED scrape terms)
Bart Torvik women's ratings (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
raw_data: women's D1 game results and box scores (possessions)
women's tournament brackets, seeds and host sites

cbb.in_season_event_format.label: In-season multi-team event format, field and draw (e.g. Players Era, Maui, Battle 4 Atlantis)
cbb.in_season_event_format.mechanism: An early-season event's champion is determined by its field, draw, format (bracket or pool play with points-differential seeding) and game spacing at a neutral site.
cbb.in_season_event_format.rationale: KXNCAAMBTOURNEY settles on such an event. Formats change by year and event: pool play with a point-differential tiebreak rewards running up margins and makes the final depend on margin, not only wins; consecutive-day games add fatigue for thin rotations. November ratings are mostly prior, so rating uncertainty is wide and the draw matters.
cbb.in_season_event_format.measurement: Per event-season record: field list, bracket or pool assignments, format rules (games per team, tiebreak order incl. point differential), venue, dates. Simulate 100,000 times with cbb.ratings_fundamentals (preseason-weighted, posterior sd as of pricing), neutral site, back-to-back penalty 1.0 pt per consecutive day for rotations of 7 or fewer, and margin draws when point differential decides seeding. As-of: format as announced before pricing.
free_sources: event organiser websites and bracket pages (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED archive)
Sports-Reference schedules with event names (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)

cbb.co_champion_expected_share.label: Expected 1/N share of a conference regular-season title
cbb.co_champion_expected_share.mechanism: A declared co-championship splits the payout, so the value of a regular-season champion contract is the expected share, determined by how often the team ties for first and with how many others.
cbb.co_champion_expected_share.rationale: Pricing the champion series as P(best record) or P(wins tiebreak) is wrong under a 1/N rule: a team that often ties for first with one rival is worth about half of its tie probability. The size of the error grows in balanced leagues where two- and three-way ties at the top are common.
cbb.co_champion_expected_share.measurement: From the joint standings simulation (cbb.conference_standings_sim, 50,000 seasons, remaining conference games only, completed results fixed as of pricing): for each simulated season let W* = best conference win-loss record and T = set of teams with that record; if the league's policy is to declare co-champions, team i's share = 1{i in T}/|T|; if it names one champion by tiebreak, share = 1{i is tiebreak winner}. Expected share = mean over simulations. Policy flag per conference from published championship policy, versioned by season.
free_sources: conference websites (championship policy, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for every league)
Sports-Reference conference standings history
raw_data: historical counts of co-champions by league

cbb.conf_tiebreak_seeding_rules.label: Conference tiebreak procedure used to seed the conference tournament
cbb.conf_tiebreak_seeding_rules.mechanism: Tied teams are ordered for tournament seeding by the league's published procedure (head-to-head, record versus the top of the standings, NET), which decides byes, campus hosting and bracket side.
cbb.conf_tiebreak_seeding_rules.rationale: REGTOP settlement ignores tiebreaks, but tournament champion and championship-game series depend on seeding: a tie for 4th decides who gets a double bye in a 15-team league, and a tie for 1st decides bracket sides for the two favourites. Ignoring the procedure assigns byes at random and misprices teams near seed-line boundaries.
cbb.conf_tiebreak_seeding_rules.measurement: Per conference-season, encode the ordered tiebreak steps as a function over simulated final standings: step list (head-to-head record among tied teams, record against teams in seeding order, NET rank on a stated date, coin flip). Apply to each simulated season from cbb.conference_standings_sim to assign seeds 1..n before simulating the tournament bracket. Versioned by publication date; unspecified steps fall back to NET rank.
free_sources: conference tournament handbooks and championship manuals on conference websites (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED availability for all leagues)
raw_data: per-conference tiebreak step lists by season

cbb.bracket_seed_statistic_sim.label: Per-simulation bracket seed statistics (upset counts, #k-seed counts by round, semifinal seed sum, maximum upset seed margin)
cbb.bracket_seed_statistic_sim.mechanism: Bracket-wide seed contracts settle on deterministic functions of all games' outcomes, so their probabilities are the empirical distributions of those functions over simulated tournaments.
cbb.bracket_seed_statistic_sim.rationale: These statistics aggregate dependent games: an early upset removes a favourite and changes later matchups, and year-specific seed-line strength gaps shift all counts together. Historical seed base rates alone ignore the current field; per-team advancement probabilities alone cannot give counts or maxima because they lose the joint structure.
cbb.bracket_seed_statistic_sim.measurement: From cbb.bracket_sim (100,000 tournaments using current ratings with posterior sd, bracket as published or simulated seeds before Selection Sunday): per simulation compute (a) for each round r and seed k, number of #k seeds reaching r and winning in r; (b) number of games in round r won by the higher numerical seed; (c) sum of official seeds of the four semifinalists; (d) max over all games of (winner seed - loser seed) where positive, with and without First Four games; (e) for each round r, the highest numerical seed reaching r (title-only KXMARMADHIGHSEED). Output the pmf of each statistic; calibrate to 1985-present seed-level history via a check of mean counts.
free_sources: NCAA.com brackets
Sports-Reference tournament history (seed-level results since 1985)
raw_data: published bracket with seeds and First Four pairings
historical tournament game results with both seeds and round
team ratings with posterior sd at pricing

cbb.coach_award_profile.label: Coach-of-the-year candidate profile: over-performance versus preseason expectation
cbb.coach_award_profile.mechanism: Coach awards are voted on how far a team outperforms what was expected of it, so the driver is the gap between realised and preseason-expected success, not team strength itself.
cbb.coach_award_profile.rationale: A model using team strength would pick coaches of the best teams, who rarely win; the award follows over-performance (wins and AP rank versus preseason poll and projection), conference titles and tournament runs, with recency weighting toward February and March. Some voters favour first-year turnarounds. This is distinct from player award profiles.
cbb.coach_award_profile.measurement: Per coach-season as of pricing: (actual win% - preseason projected win%) from preseason ratings, (preseason AP rank - current AP rank, unranked = 35), conference finish versus preseason conference poll, first-year flag, projected end-of-season values from the season simulation. Fit a multinomial logit on past Naismith/AP COTY winners and finalists (2000-present) with these features; output P(win) per coach, renormalised over active candidates.
free_sources: Naismith Awards website (winners, finalists; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED history)
AP poll archives on Sports-Reference
preseason conference polls on conference websites
raw_data: past COTY winners and finalists by year
preseason projections and final records by team

cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.label: KenPom AdjEM gap density around the target rank
cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.mechanism: A rank contract is decided by the order statistics of ~360 AdjEM values; what matters is the AdjEM distance to the neighbouring ranks, not the absolute rating.
cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.rationale: Near #25 teams are separated by a few tenths of a point of AdjEM while near #1 the gap can be a point or more, so identical rating noise moves a top-25 contract far more than a #1 contract. A team at #40 can be closer to the line in expected moves than a team at #28 if the intermediate teams are bunched.
cbb.kenpom_adjem_gap_density.measurement: At each daily snapshot sort AdjEM and compute for the target team gap_up = AdjEM(rank r-1) - AdjEM(team) and gap_down = AdjEM(team) - AdjEM(rank r+1), plus the number of teams within +/-0.5 AdjEM. Divide each gap by sigma_rel = sqrt(var_team + var_neighbour), where each team's variance to Mar 15 sums its own games_left times per-game update variance (cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity), its season drift variance (cbb.kenpom_prior_drift) and an opponent re-adjustment term estimated from days without a game. For top-25 use the 25th-26th boundary. As-of: last snapshot before pricing.
free_sources: Bart Torvik T-Rank (free proxy)
KenPom main ratings table (believed free to view; unverified)
raw_data: daily AdjEM for all D1 teams

cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.label: Per-game AdjEM update sensitivity
cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.mechanism: KenPom's rating is a running opponent-adjusted efficiency margin, so one game moves it by (game-level adjusted margin minus current rating) weighted by 1/games played, with opponent strength and venue entering the game-level number.
cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.rationale: A game's weight falls as games accumulate (assumed near 1/g, to be fitted), so a team moves about a point per game in November and a few tenths in March; the move is zero in expectation when the team performs at its rating. Recency and blowout treatment are not public, which is the subtle part.
cbb.kenpom_game_update_sensitivity.measurement: Fit on daily snapshot pairs from the prior three seasons: dAdjEM_team,t = w(g) * (adjusted game margin per 100 possessions - AdjEM_t-1) + opponent-feedback term, with g games played; estimate w(g), a recency multiplier, and a blowout cap by least squares. Output expected move and sd per game as a function of g, opponent AdjEM and location. Validate: out-of-sample RMSE of next-day AdjEM below 0.15. As-of: snapshots before the game.
free_sources: Bart Torvik daily T-Rank archives
KenPom (subscription)
Sports-Reference game logs

cbb.kenpom_snapshot_timing_rules.label: KenPom snapshot timing and counting rules
cbb.kenpom_snapshot_timing_rules.mechanism: The contract reads the ratings page at 12:00pm 'EST' on Monday Mar 15, 2027, so which Selection Sunday results the overnight refresh processed, whether EST means fixed offset or New York clock time, and downtime decide the exact state.
cbb.kenpom_snapshot_timing_rules.rationale: Mar 15, 2027 is the day after US daylight time starts and the day after Selection Sunday, with no D1 games scheduled until the Opening Round on Mar 16. Literal EST would be 1pm EDT. Late Sunday conference finals are normally processed overnight, but a delayed refresh or downtime could leave them out for a team sitting at a cutoff.
cbb.kenpom_snapshot_timing_rules.measurement: For each past season capture the ratings page every 30 minutes from 00:00 to 14:00 ET on the Monday after Selection Sunday (archive captures where available); record the timestamp at which the last Sunday final appears in the games-played count, refresh times and downtime. Feature per team: played_on_selection_sunday flag x P(final unprocessed at 12:00 ET or 13:00 ET), using the historical refresh-time distribution. Capture both 12:00 and 13:00 ET pages on the settlement date.
free_sources: own_capture of the KenPom ratings page (main table believed free to view; unverified)
Internet Archive captures
NCAA and conference schedule listings for Sunday final tip times

cbb.kenpom_prior_drift.label: KenPom season-horizon rating drift and preseason-prior phase-out
cbb.kenpom_prior_drift.mechanism: Between a November pricing date and Mar 15 a team's AdjEM moves because the preseason prior is phased out and its error revealed, and because true strength drifts with roster integration, injuries and shooting-luck regression.
cbb.kenpom_prior_drift.rationale: For most of the contract's life this variance, not the last week's games, decides rank probabilities. It is larger for high-churn rosters (low returning minutes, many transfers) and for teams with weakly connected schedules, and its expected sign can be predicted from three-point luck and the gap between prior and results-only ratings.
cbb.kenpom_prior_drift.measurement: From stored daily ratings for the prior 5 seasons (KenPom archive if licensed, else Torvik T-Rank as proxy), compute D = AdjEM(Mar 15 equivalent: Monday after Selection Sunday) - AdjEM(d) per team for each pricing date d. Regress |D| and D on games remaining, preseason-prior weight at d (KenPom's stated phase-out, else estimated as the AdjEM gap between prior-inclusive and results-only ratings), returning-minutes share and transfer minutes (cbb.roster_minutes), own/opponent three-point luck (cbb.three_pt_luck) and schedule connectivity; output mean drift and sd per team-date, in AdjEM points per 100 possessions. As-of: ratings captured at d; no later revision used.
free_sources: Bart Torvik T-Rank daily archives
Sports-Reference rosters and game logs
KenPom ratings archive (subscription)

cbb.race_possession_alternation_model.label: Possession-alternation first-passage model
cbb.race_possession_alternation_model.mechanism: Both teams get nearly equal possessions in the opening minutes, so the first to N points is decided by points-per-possession draws on alternating possessions, with ties in possession count broken by who has the ball first.
cbb.race_possession_alternation_model.rationale: With about one point per possession a race to 10 is a 9-to-11 possession event; the team starting with the ball reaches N first whenever both need the same number of possessions, a built-in edge of a few points of probability. Offensive rebounds and turnovers break strict alternation, so the edge shrinks as N grows and with offensive-rebound rate.
cbb.race_possession_alternation_model.measurement: From play-by-play of 5 prior seasons estimate for each team in the opening segment the distribution of points per possession (outcomes 0,1,2,3,4 with free throws), the offensive-rebound continuation rate and opening turnover rate with shrinkage n/(n+15) to the opponent-adjusted conference mean. Tip model: P(tip win) = logistic(a + b*height difference of the expected jumpers + c*shrunk historical tip-win rate of each jumper from 'Jump Ball won by' play-by-play lines, shrinkage n/(n+10) to 0.5). Simulate 50,000 races for N = 10, 25, 50 with alternating possessions; output P(A first | possession A), P(A first | possession B) and their mixture by P(tip win), set to 1 or 0 once the tip is known. As-of: lineup-confirmed time before tip.
free_sources: Sports-Reference play-by-play (limited)
ESPN play-by-play JSON
NCAA stats site
raw_data: play-by-play with scoring sequence and possession flag
opening tip winner and jumper names

cbb.race_n_threshold_scaling.label: Race-N threshold scaling and win-link
cbb.race_n_threshold_scaling.mechanism: The mapping from team scoring rate to winning the race changes with N: at 10 it is mostly opening variance, at 25 it is a half-way runs contest, and at 50 it approaches the share of points over about 26 minutes and can span the halftime break.
cbb.race_n_threshold_scaling.rationale: Because sd of the points gap grows like the square root of possessions while the mean grows linearly, the favourite's chance rises with N toward its win probability. A team that wins by defence may lose the race to 50 if it scores slowly, so offence level and not margin is the driver.
cbb.race_n_threshold_scaling.measurement: From historical play-by-play compute for N in {10,25,50} the minute each team reaches N and whether it led the race; fit logit P(race win N) = a_N + b_N * (AdjO_A/AdjD_B-based expected points per possession difference) by N with team-level random effects, and record the median time to N and share of games where N is reached after halftime. As-of: ratings snapshot before tip, five seasons of games.
free_sources: Sports-Reference play-by-play
ESPN play-by-play JSON
Bart Torvik game data
raw_data: time and score at each scoring event

cbb.race_live_state.label: Live race state: points to N, possession and clock
cbb.race_live_state.mechanism: After tip the probability of reaching N first is a first-passage from the current state: each team's remaining points to N, who has the ball, game clock and the units on the floor.
cbb.race_live_state.rationale: Used only if the market trades in play, which the evidence does not show. Then state dominates pregame inputs, a single three changes the price sharply, and latency between the live feed and quotes is the practical edge or risk.
cbb.race_live_state.measurement: At each play-by-play event t: need_A = N - score_A(t), need_B = N - score_B(t), possession flag, seconds elapsed, foul/bonus state, on-floor unit ids. P(A first) = simulation from the state with the alternation model's per-possession point distributions for the current units (10,000 paths). Record feed latency = quote timestamp - event timestamp. As-of: event time; never use events after the quote time.
free_sources: ESPN live play-by-play JSON (unofficial, delayed)
NCAA live stats (stats.ncaa.org game pages)

cbb.stat_leader_qualification_tracker.label: NCAA minimum-qualification tracker for leaderboard eligibility
cbb.stat_leader_qualification_tracker.mechanism: A player leads the official per-game list only if he meets the NCAA minimum (a share of team games or a minimum total of the stat), so a missed-games run turns a leading average into a non-qualifier and removes him from the max.
cbb.stat_leader_qualification_tracker.rationale: Qualification is a cliff, not a slope: a player averaging 24 ppg who has missed too many games is not eligible, while the next qualifying player wins. Thresholds differ by category and are set by the NCAA, and postseason games raise the team-games denominator.
cbb.stat_leader_qualification_tracker.measurement: For each candidate and category compute games_played, team_games_played, projected team games including the expected postseason pmf from cbb.team_postseason_games_projection (conference tournament, NCAA, NIT, Crown, CBI, CIT) and the stat-specific NCAA minimum from the current NCAA statistics rules; the feature is P(qualify) = P(games played over remaining team games >= required share) using the player's per-game availability probability from cbb.dnp_cause_taxonomy, and distance in games to the threshold. As-of: recomputed after each team game.
free_sources: NCAA statistics rules and leaderboards (stats.ncaa.org)
Sports-Reference player pages

cbb.stat_leader_source_reconciliation.label: Official stat feed reconciliation and update lag
cbb.stat_leader_source_reconciliation.mechanism: The rules count all official games including non-NCAA postseason events, but the usual leaderboard source may lag, may exclude events such as the College Basketball Crown, and can differ from box scores by stat corrections.
cbb.stat_leader_source_reconciliation.rationale: A season-long contract is settled off one table after the last game; differences of 0.1 to 0.3 per game between sources can decide a close race for threes made or rebounds, and the postseason inclusion list goes beyond NCAA-sanctioned events.
cbb.stat_leader_source_reconciliation.measurement: For the 3 most recent seasons collect the final per-game value for top-20 players in each category from the NCAA site, the relevant conference office's statistics page, Sports-Reference and ESPN; compute pairwise absolute differences, the minimum-games rule each table applies, whether conference tables split conference-only games, the date each becomes final, and whether Crown, CBI and CIT games are included. source_gap_i = max pairwise difference; flag when the rank 1-2 gap is below it or when the conference and NCAA tables name different leaders. As-of: weekly in season, daily at the end.
free_sources: NCAA statistics site
Conference office statistics pages
Sports-Reference
ESPN player stats pages

cbb.leader_average_inertia.label: Leaderboard average inertia and remaining-swing bound
cbb.leader_average_inertia.mechanism: A season average changes by exactly (x - mean)/(g+1) after a game with value x, so the games remaining limit how far the gap between the leader and challengers can close, and late in the season a lead is close to locked.
