cbb.leader_average_inertia.rationale: At 25 games played one 40-point game raises a 20 ppg average by under 0.8, and a challenger 1.5 ppg back needs several far above average games, so the effective uncertainty falls as 1/g; postseason games add few extra samples, which matters most for players on deep-tournament teams.
cbb.leader_average_inertia.measurement: For each pair (leader, challenger) compute the gap in current average, the number of games remaining for each (regular-season schedule plus expected postseason), the per-game sd, and the swing bound d = (mu_challenger - mu_leader) * G_rem/(g+G_rem) plus the standard error sqrt(G_rem) * sd/(g+G_rem). The feature is z = (gap - expected_catch_up)/se. As-of: updated after every game by either player.
free_sources: Sports-Reference game logs
NCAA statistics site

cbb.team_postseason_games_projection.label: Projected postseason games per team (conference tournament, NCAA, NIT, Crown, CBI, CIT)
cbb.team_postseason_games_projection.mechanism: All official postseason games count, so a candidate's team's postseason game count adds samples to his average and raises the team-games denominator used for NCAA qualification.
cbb.team_postseason_games_projection.rationale: A team's run length varies from one conference-tournament game to about ten games, depending on strength, seed, byes, NCAA selection and invitational events. The Crown, CBI and CIT are invitational, so participation is partly a team choice and not simulable from ratings alone.
cbb.team_postseason_games_projection.measurement: From cbb.bracket_sim (market-free strength posterior from cbb.ratings_fundamentals): pmf of conference-tournament games by seed and bye (cbb.conference_standings_sim, cbb.auto_bid_structure), P(NCAA bid) and expected NCAA rounds, P(NIT bid | no NCAA bid) by rating rank, and P(Crown/CBI/CIT) from historical participation rates of non-NIT teams by rating rank and conference (5 prior seasons). Output pmf of total postseason games per team. As-of: ratings through the prior day; recomputed weekly and daily in March.
free_sources: Bart Torvik T-Rank
NCAA and conference bracket pages
Sports-Reference postseason results

cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.label: Coaching vacancy search state: opening date, decision-makers, search firm and interim arrangement
cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.mechanism: A hire is the end of a search process run by an athletic director, sometimes a president or board and often a search firm; how far the search has progressed bounds both timing and candidate set.
cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.rationale: Searches opened by a firing late in a season move fast and usually finish within weeks, but a retirement announced just before a season can be followed by a deliberately deferred search while an interim coaches the whole season; in that regime days since the vacancy carry almost no information and the interim's season does. Subtle: a school can announce the search start in the opening press release, and that single field decides which timing regime applies; the stage of the search (interviews reported, finalist count) then shifts probability between named and unnamed candidates.
cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.measurement: Per vacancy, as-of timestamp t: opening date and cause (fired, resigned, retired, left for another job), announced search start date or rule ('begins after the season', 'immediately', none stated), search_start_lag = announced search start minus opening date in days, days since the SEARCH opened (floored at 0 while the school says the search has not begun; this, not days since the vacancy, indexes every conversion and residual curve), whether an interim is named, who, and for what span (rest of season or until a hire), AD tenure in years, search firm named (yes/no, which firm), count of publicly reported interviewed candidates and finalists at t, whether a board/regent approval meeting is scheduled; each field carries the first public report timestamp, never backfilled.
free_sources: University athletics press releases
ESPN college basketball news
Local newspaper coverage
raw_data: vacancy table: school, opening_date, cause, interim_coach, interim_span, announced_search_start, AD_name, AD_start_date, search_firm, board_meeting_dates
report log: timestamp, outlet, candidate, stage (contacted/interviewed/finalist/offer)

cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.label: Head-coach candidate track record, opponent-adjusted and resource-adjusted
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.mechanism: Hiring committees choose among candidates largely on demonstrated programme-building: rating improvement over predecessor, tournament results, recruiting/portal success and conduct record.
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.rationale: A candidate's raw win-loss record mixes coaching value with programme resources; schools ranking candidates (and reporters naming them) favour coaches whose teams outperform their budget and conference. Subtle: one deep NCAA run inflates perceived value far more than multi-year efficiency gains, so both should be measured.
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.measurement: For each candidate: seasons as head coach; mean change in adjusted efficiency margin (point-in-time end-of-season Torvik/KenPom) versus the three seasons before arrival; NCAA bids, tournament wins and Sweet 16s in last 5 seasons; resource-adjusted margin = residual of adjusted margin on conference and athletic budget; for assistants: years as top assistant and head-coach tree; shrink single-season effects with weight n/(n+3) seasons.
free_sources: Sports-Reference coach pages
Barttorvik historical team ratings
Knight Commission / USA Today athletic finance database
raw_data: coach career table: coach, school, season, role, W-L, tournament result
end-of-season adjusted efficiency margin by team-season

cbb.candidate_program_ties.label: Candidate ties to the programme, athletic director and conference region
cbb.candidate_program_ties.mechanism: Hires disproportionately go to coaches with prior links: alumni, former assistants of the programme, previous hires of the same AD, coaches already in the region or recruiting footprint.
cbb.candidate_program_ties.rationale: Ties lower information and negotiation costs and are a strong prior over candidate identity; they also explain why a less-accomplished candidate may beat a better record. Subtle: the AD's own career history (schools worked at, previous coaching hires) is often more predictive than the candidate's ties to the school itself.
cbb.candidate_program_ties.measurement: Binary and count features per candidate-school pair: alumnus (played/graduated), former staff member (years, role), previous hire or colleague of the current AD (matched through AD career history), same agent as other staff, head-coaching job within 500 miles or in the same conference footprint; computed from public biographies as of t.
free_sources: University staff biographies
Wikipedia coach and AD career pages
Sports-Reference coach pages
raw_data: AD career history and list of prior coaching hires

cbb.program_hiring_resources.label: Programme hiring resources: salary pool, buyout capacity, revenue-sharing and NIL budget
cbb.program_hiring_resources.mechanism: Whether a school can land a sitting head coach depends on salary it can offer, its ability to pay that coach's buyout, and the roster budget (revenue sharing and NIL collective) it can promise.
cbb.program_hiring_resources.rationale: Since the 2025 House settlement, roster budget is a central selling point; a sitting coach with a large buyout is only reachable by schools willing to pay it. Subtle: the outgoing coach's own buyout or retirement terms consume the same budget and can push a school toward cheaper assistants.
cbb.program_hiring_resources.measurement: As of t: predecessor's salary and buyout owed (from public contract/FOIA records), reported maximum offer, each candidate's current salary and buyout amount with step-down dates, school athletic revenue (latest fiscal year), basketball share of revenue-sharing allocation where disclosed; express candidate reachability as offer_capacity / (candidate_salary + candidate_buyout).
free_sources: USA Today college basketball coach salary database
Public-records contract disclosures
Knight Commission finance database
raw_data: coach contract table: coach, salary, term, buyout schedule by date
school athletic revenue/expense by fiscal year

cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.label: Candidate availability calendar: current-team season status, buyout step-downs and pro-league timing
cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.mechanism: A candidate coaching a team still alive in the NCAA tournament, an NBA assistant in the playoffs, or one whose buyout drops on a set date is effectively unavailable until that event passes.
cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.rationale: Searches either wait for a preferred candidate or move on; this changes both who is hired and when. Subtle: transfer-portal windows push schools to hire before the portal opens, which penalises candidates whose teams advance deep in March.
cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.measurement: Per candidate as of t: current team's elimination status and earliest elimination date (from bracket simulation), buyout step-down dates and amounts, NBA team playoff status for NBA assistants; per school: transfer-portal opening date and days remaining; feature = expected days until candidate is free versus expected days until school wants a hire.
free_sources: NCAA tournament bracket and results
NBA playoff schedule
Public coach contracts (buyout schedules)

cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.label: Timestamped coaching-search report ledger with source reliability and report-to-hire conversion
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.mechanism: Insider reports (interviewed, finalist, offer, agreement in principle) are noisy but increasingly informative signals; their historical conversion to actual hires depends on outlet, report stage and lead time.
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.rationale: Most of the information about a search arrives as reports, and a single credible agreement report moves the outcome near certainty; but early lists of names include many that never had serious contact. Subtle: candidates and agents leak interest to gain leverage at their current school, so 'interest' reports convert far less than 'finalist' or 'offer' reports.
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.measurement: Log every public report with timestamp (UTC), outlet and reporter, candidate, stage in {linked, contacted, interviewed, finalist, offer, agreement, denial}; estimate historical conversion P(hired | stage, outlet tier) from past D1 power-conference searches (at least 5 cycles), shrunk toward stage mean with weight n/(n+10); denial reports from the candidate tracked separately with their own conversion rate.
free_sources: ESPN, CBS Sports and The Athletic reporting
X/Twitter posts of national insiders (capture timestamps)
Local beat reporters
raw_data: report log: ts, outlet, reporter, candidate, stage, link

cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.label: Residual probability mass for unlisted candidates and for no permanent hire by the cutoff
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.mechanism: The multi-outcome contract lists named candidates only; the true distribution includes an 'other' mass (a candidate not listed) and a 'no permanent hire before deadline' mass.
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.rationale: Listed-candidate probabilities must sum to at most 1 minus these masses; historically many hires are names that were not among the earliest-reported candidates. Subtle: the 'other' mass shrinks quickly as the search progresses and reports concentrate, so it is time-varying.
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.measurement: From past searches: fraction of hires that were not among the first N publicly linked names at days d since the SEARCH opened (d = 0, 7, 14, 30; the clock is held at 0 until the announced search start, using search_start_lag from the vacancy-state input), estimated as a curve with binomial confidence bands; no-hire mass = P(no vacancy exists by the cutoff, from the incumbent hazard input) + P(search not concluding by Sep 1, 2027 given its start date) + probability that the interim is made permanent (counted for the interim's own market, not for the residual) or that only an interim or coach-in-waiting is named; as-of t.
free_sources: Historical search coverage (ESPN, CBS) reconstructed by date
raw_data: per past search: opening date, candidate link dates, hire identity and date

cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.label: Candidate eligibility constraints: NCAA show-cause orders, pending infractions and legal or conduct issues
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.mechanism: A show-cause penalty, pending infractions case or conduct investigation makes most schools unwilling or unable to hire a candidate during its term.
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.rationale: This removes names that a pure track-record ranking would rate highly. Subtle: show-cause orders allow hiring with restrictions, and some schools accept the restrictions; the term end date matters relative to the cutoff.
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.measurement: Per candidate: active NCAA show-cause (start, end, restrictions) from NCAA infractions decisions database; open infractions case flag; public conduct investigations; binary 'constrained at t' and days until constraint lapses.
free_sources: NCAA Legislative Services infractions decisions database
News coverage of investigations
raw_data: infractions decisions: person, penalty, start/end dates

cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.label: Interim coach's in-season audition: results versus preseason expectation and interim-to-permanent base rate
cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.mechanism: When an interim coaches the whole season before the search opens, the team's results under him are the main game-driven route to the permanent job: a clear beat of expectation, a conference finish above projection or an NCAA run turns the interim into a leading candidate or lets the school skip a search.
cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.rationale: Search timing and candidate ranking are set partly by what happens on the court during the deferred-search window. A promoted assistant inherits a roster chosen by the departed coach, so the fair comparison is results against a fundamentals-only expectation, not raw wins; a late-season run also raises the interim's profile with the AD and fan base. Subtle: interim promotions are rare enough that the base rate is tiny-sample, and a poor season can end the interim's case quickly.
cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.measurement: For the interim coach at as-of t: games coached, AdjEM_fund results-versus-expectation = mean over games of (actual margin - cbb.ratings_fundamentals pregame expected margin), shrunk with weight n/(n+12) games toward 0; end-of-season gap between final fundamentals rating and the preseason prior from cbb.preseason_prior; projected conference finish and NCAA bid, seed and round-reached probabilities from cbb.bracket_sim; promotion base rate = share of past D1 interim or acting coaches who coached a full or most of a season (at least 15 games) and were then named permanent, split by whether the team met its preseason expectation (pooled over every available season, shrunk to the pooled mean with weight n/(n+8)); no betting line or price enters any term.
free_sources: Barttorvik T-Rank game results and ratings
Sports-Reference coach and team pages
NCAA bracket and results
Wikipedia and university press releases for historical interim coaches
raw_data: interim coach table: school, season, coach, games_coached, named_permanent flag
game results with pregame fundamentals expected margin
preseason prior rating and final rating by team-season

cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.label: Incumbent head-coach departure hazard and succession arrangements
cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.mechanism: A next-coach market can only pay out after a vacancy exists; before one does, the probability of any listed name is the probability of a vacancy before the cutoff times the conditional hire probability, and a pre-arranged coach-in-waiting changes the conditional distribution.
cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.rationale: For a template opened on a programme with a sitting coach, the dominant term is the chance the incumbent leaves (retirement, firing, a better job, health), driven by age, contract length, tenure, results against expectation and public succession statements. Subtle: retirements are lumpy around season ends and are often announced with a named successor, which concentrates mass on one name and removes the search entirely.
cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.measurement: For each sitting head coach at t: age, years remaining on contract, tenure, last three seasons' fundamentals-rating results versus preseason prior, conference and tournament results, reported health or retirement statements, announced coach-in-waiting or succession plan (flag with first report timestamp); hazard h(coach) = logistic fit of departure within 12 months on those covariates over at least 15 past seasons of all D1 head coaches, shrunk toward the age-band base rate with weight n/(n+25) coach-seasons; output P(vacancy opens before the cutoff date) and P(named successor already exists | vacancy).
free_sources: Sports-Reference coach pages
USA Today coach salary database
Wikipedia coach career pages
University athletics announcements
raw_data: coach-season table: school, coach, age, contract_end, tenure, departure flag and cause

cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.label: Coach end-game decision policy when trailing by 2 or 3 or leading by 3 in the final possessions
cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.mechanism: Whether a trailing team goes for the tying two or the winning three, and whether a leader up 3 fouls or defends, decides how much probability lands exactly on a tie at the buzzer.
cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.rationale: The tie probability at the end of regulation is not just the density of a smooth margin at zero: in close games the final possessions are strategic, and a coach who reliably plays for overtime raises the tie mass while one who plays for the win shifts it to plus or minus one. Subtle: holding for the last shot when tied converts a tied game into either a win or overtime, so possession at the tie matters.
cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.measurement: From play-by-play, for each coach (and pooled by tier): in possessions starting with under 35 seconds left and team trailing by 2, share of final shot attempts that are twos; when trailing by 3, share of threes versus quick twos; when leading by 3 with under 10 seconds, foul rate; shrink coach rates to the pooled rate with weight n/(n+15) situations over the last 5 seasons; convert to a tie-mass multiplier on P(margin=0 at 0:00). Because qualifying situations are only a handful per coach-season, use the tier-level pooled rate by default and let a coach deviate only when his shrunk rate differs from the pooled rate by more than two standard errors.
free_sources: hoopR / sportsdataverse play-by-play
ESPN play-by-play JSON
raw_data: play-by-play: game_id, period, clock, score, team, event type, shot value, foul flag

cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.label: Player-foul and team-foul carryover into overtime and resulting lineup depletion
cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.mechanism: Player fouls and second-half team fouls carry into overtime, so teams entering OT have players near or at the five-foul limit and are already in the bonus, changing scoring variance in each five-minute period.
cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.rationale: Repeat ties depend on how many points are scored per OT period and how lumpy they are: bonus free throws add frequent one- and two-point scores, and fouled-out starters lower efficiency unevenly. Subtle: the carryover makes later OT periods progressively more foul-driven, so per-period tie probability is not constant across periods.
cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.measurement: Rule version assumed (unverified for 2026-27, see ot_u3): men's two 20-minute halves, five personal fouls to disqualify, team-foul bonus carrying from the second half into overtime periods, five-minute overtimes; store a rule_version flag per game and fit only on seasons with the same structure. From play-by-play for all OT games: at the start of each OT period, count players with 4 and 5 fouls per team (weighted by their minutes share), team-foul count and bonus status; points per team per OT period and distribution of scoring events by value; estimate P(tie after OT k | depletion state) by logistic fit pooled over 10 seasons; pregame proxy = team foul rate and bench depth.
free_sources: hoopR / sportsdataverse play-by-play
Sports-Reference box scores with OT
raw_data: play-by-play fouls with player id and period
box score minutes and fouls per player

cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.label: Live score, clock, period, possession and foul state for in-play overtime pricing
cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.mechanism: Once a game is close late or in overtime, the rung probability is set by the current score difference, time left, possession, team-foul bonus status and players near five fouls, and the pregame margin model becomes nearly irrelevant.
cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.rationale: The 2+ and 3+ rungs sit near zero until regulation is tied or in extra time; if the market trades during the game, almost all price movement comes from the live state. Subtle: a tie at the final buzzer needs both possession and timing, and an overtime already in progress changes the remaining number of required ties by one for each rung; free live feeds can lag, so the data latency itself is a modelling input.
cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.measurement: At as-of t during the game: period, seconds remaining, score margin, possession, team fouls and bonus status for both teams, count of players with 4 fouls and fouled-out players, OT index k already played; P(rung N | state) = P(tie at end of current period | state) x P_tie_OT^(N-k-1) using a state-based first-passage model on the margin (fit on play-by-play with state buckets: margin -6..+6, clock 60 s bins in the last 5 minutes); record feed latency (seconds from event to capture) and discard states older than the latency budget.
free_sources: ESPN public JSON live scoreboard and play-by-play (latency unverified)
hoopR / sportsdataverse play-by-play (historical, for model fit)
raw_data: live play-by-play: timestamp, period, clock, score, possession, team fouls, player fouls
capture-time stamps to measure feed latency

cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.label: Expected tournament games per candidate player (field entry x team survival x availability)
cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.mechanism: A player can only hit a milestone in games his team plays; expected exposure is the sum over rounds of P(team in field) times P(team reaches that round) times P(player active).
cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.rationale: Total team-games in the tournament are fixed by the format, but they concentrate on strong teams; a star on a 1 seed averages several games, a star on a 16 seed one or two. Subtle: the First Four counts, so play-in teams add a game, and a changed field size changes the count. The market trades through the tournament window, so exposure must be recomputed as teams are eliminated and as a milestone either occurs (settling YES) or becomes unreachable with fewer games left.
cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.measurement: For each player as of t: E[games] = sum_r P(team bid) * P(team plays round r | bid) * P(player active in r), using the bracket simulation with fundamentals-only ratings; P(active) from injury status and star injury risk; before Selection Sunday include bid probability; report full distribution of games (1 to 7, or more under an expanded field). In-tournament state: after the field is set, condition on the live bracket at t (teams still alive, games already played, results to date) and set P(YES) = 1 for the relevant series once any qualifying game is final; remaining exposure = games still to be played by surviving teams only.
free_sources: Barttorvik tournament projections (T-Rank)
NCAA bracket and results
raw_data: bracket simulation output: team, round, probability

cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.label: Player single-game scoring right-tail index (probability of 40+ and 50+ point games)
cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.mechanism: A 50-point game sits far beyond typical college means, so its probability depends on the right tail of the player's game scoring distribution, driven by volume ceiling (shot attempts, free-throw trips) and hot shooting.
cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.rationale: Mean and sd from a negative binomial understate extreme tails for high-usage shooters and overstate them for efficient interior scorers. Subtle: extreme games usually combine high attempts, a hot three-point night and extra minutes (overtime), so the tail is a compound of several stages, not a single scale parameter.
cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.measurement: Per player: fit a compound model points = minutes x usage-based attempts x points per attempt with Beta-uncertain shooting and NB attempt dispersion, on the last 2 seasons of game logs; validate tail mass against observed 35+/40+ frequencies of D1 players pooled by role (generalised Pareto fit above 30 points, threshold chosen by mean-excess plot); output P(points >= 50 | game played) with credible interval. Attempt volume is scaled by the ratio of matchup expected possessions (cbb.tempo) to the possessions of the player's logged games.
free_sources: Barttorvik player game logs
Sports-Reference player game logs
hoopR box scores
raw_data: player game logs: minutes, FGA, 3PA, FTA, points

cbb.triple_double_joint_propensity.label: Player per-game triple-double propensity across points, rebounds, assists, blocks and steals
cbb.triple_double_joint_propensity.mechanism: A triple-double needs 10+ in three of five categories in one game, which depends on the player's joint distribution of these counts given minutes, not their marginal means.
cbb.triple_double_joint_propensity.rationale: Points-rebounds-assists versatile guards and forwards and points-rebounds-blocks rim protectors are the realistic candidates; the joint probability is driven by positive correlation through minutes and pace and by negative correlation between assists and rebounds for some roles. Subtle: near misses (8-9 in a third category) are far more frequent and are the most informative for calibration.
cbb.triple_double_joint_propensity.measurement: Per player: simulate 5-category counts with NB marginals conditioned on a shared minutes draw and a Gaussian copula of residual correlations (from player stat covariance shrunk to role with n/(n+40)); count share of simulated games with >=3 categories at 10+; calibrate against observed D1 triple-double and 'two 10s plus 8+' frequencies over the last 5 seasons; as-of: prior games only. Counts are scaled by the same matchup-possessions ratio before the copula draw.
free_sources: Barttorvik player game logs
Sports-Reference player game logs (single-game finder is a paid Stathead product; coverage start unverified)
hoopR box scores
raw_data: player box scores: points, rebounds, assists, blocks, steals, minutes

cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.label: Any-player union over all tournament player-games with dependence
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.mechanism: YES = at least one player-game hits the milestone; probability is one minus the probability that none does, computed over correlated player-games in a bracket where survival paths are shared.
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.rationale: Simple independence summation overstates YES when probability is concentrated on a few stars whose games are correlated by team survival, and the chance that a candidate's team loses early removes several of his games at once. Subtle: the event is dominated by a handful of players, so the union is sensitive to errors in their tails, and 'long tail' depth (many players at very small probabilities) still contributes.
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.measurement: Monte Carlo: simulate the bracket (with First Four) N >= 50,000 times; for each simulated game draw active players' stat lines from their per-game models (minutes linked to game margin and OT); YES if any line hits the milestone; report P(YES) and the contribution share of the top 10 players; compare with the analytical 1 - prod(1 - p_i)^{E[games_i]} as a check.
free_sources: Derived from bracket simulation and player models

cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.label: Star minutes ceiling in single-elimination tournament games
cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.mechanism: In elimination games coaches shorten rotations and play stars close to the full 40 minutes in close games, while lopsided first-round games cut star minutes.
cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.rationale: Milestones need volume; a star's minutes distribution in the tournament differs from the regular season, with more 38+ minute games in close contests and longer media timeouts in televised tournament games giving extra rest. Subtle: overtime adds five minutes at a time and appears more often in close tournament games.
cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.measurement: From the last 10 tournaments: for each team's top two usage players, minutes distribution in tournament games versus their own regular-season distribution, split by final margin bucket (0-5, 6-12, 13+); estimate shift in mean and in P(minutes >= 38); apply per candidate via role and coach rotation length.
free_sources: Sports-Reference tournament box scores

cbb.tournament_field_milestone_base_rate.label: Field-level tournament base rate of 50-point games and triple-doubles by era
cbb.tournament_field_milestone_base_rate.mechanism: The any-player event is a rare count over about 67 team-games (more player-games), so the historical per-tournament frequency of 50+ point games and triple-doubles, adjusted for era, is a direct calibration anchor for the bottom-up union.
cbb.tournament_field_milestone_base_rate.rationale: Per-player tail models extrapolate far beyond their data; a field-level anchor bounds them. Era matters: the shot clock (35 s from 1993-94, 30 s from 2015-16), the three-point line and its 2019-20 move back, and tournament size changed scoring volume and the number of games, and stat-recording practice for assists and rebounds changed. Subtle: with so few events per decade the anchor is a wide interval, not a point, and it must not be tuned to the 2026 outcome.
cbb.tournament_field_milestone_base_rate.measurement: Count, per tournament year since 1985 (all rounds, play-in games from 2011), the number of player-games with 50+ points and with three 10+ categories among points, rebounds, assists, blocks and steals (blocks and steals only where recorded); events per 1,000 player-games with minutes above 25; Beta-Binomial posterior per era block (pre-1994, 1994-2014, 2015-present) with a Beta(0.5, 500) weakly informative prior; anchor P(YES in one tournament) = 1 - (1 - r_era)^(player-games with minutes above 25 in the target format), reported with its 90 percent interval and compared with the bottom-up cbb.milestone_union_aggregation output; as-of: tournaments completed before the pricing date only.

The same rating gap converts into a larger expected margin in a high-possession game and a smaller one in a low-possession game, so the spread is gap times possession ratio, and the underdog's cover chance is higher in slow games where margin sd is also smaller relative to the number.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress realised margin on gap, possessions and gap x possessions using prior-season games; check whether residual sd falls with sqrt(possessions) and whether the gap coefficient scales with tempo.

interactions.hypothesis: Once the expected margin passes roughly 15 to 20 points the game flips into a blowout regime whose end-of-game compression depends on the coach: a lead-protecting coach turns a model margin of 25 into a 14 point cover miss, while a starter-heavy coach does not. Below the threshold the coach term is irrelevant.
interactions.how_to_test: Split games by predicted margin bucket and compare final-margin minus lead-at-8-minutes across coaches with high and low decay; verify the difference vanishes below 12 points.

interactions.hypothesis: Early in the season (before about 8 games) the prior carries the weight and uncertainty is highest, so the weight on the in-season improvement slope should be near zero; by February the same slope is a useful signal. The correct blend depends on games played and on roster continuity.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare out-of-sample margin error of the gap using prior-only, ratings-only and blended versions in game-number buckets (0-5, 6-12, 13-20, 21+) and test for a crossing point. cbb.in_season_improvement is audited WEAK, so it enters only as a held-out add-on: drop it if its incremental out-of-sample log-loss gain over the two-term (uncertainty x prior) model is not positive in at least 3 of the last 5 seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: A starter's absence costs more points for a team with a short rotation and a low-quality replacement than for a deep team; the effect is also larger when the missing player controls the ball, since the replacement changes turnovers and pace as well as scoring.
interactions.how_to_test: Using games with known absences, regress margin shift on player impact value interacted with bench-depth index and replacement impact; compare to a flat per-player shift.

interactions.hypothesis: Home advantage is a three-regime piecewise term: full home court, neutral floor, and semi-home (conference tournaments held in a nearby arena); the team-specific deviation applies to the full-home regime and shrinks toward zero otherwise.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate separate venue coefficients by regime from historical margins and test whether team-specific home edges survive out of sample only in the home regime.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped probit link from rating gap to win probability; fat tails in lopsided matchups
nonlinearities.why: A 20-point expected margin is not a 99.9 percent win in practice because rating error, an injury scenario or a cold-shooting night keep upset mass near 1 to 4 percent; with a normal link the tail is understated.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold near 15 to 20 expected margin points above which lead decay appears
nonlinearities.why: Cover probabilities for big favourites fall sharply once the game is expected to be non-competitive because coaches clear benches; below the threshold the effect is zero, which is why a linear term fails.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating decay with games played (approximately 1/sqrt(n)), floor from roster change
nonlinearities.why: Posterior sd falls fast over the first 8 to 10 games and slowly afterwards, with a floor because injuries and rotation changes keep re-introducing uncertainty; treating it as constant overstates early certainty.

mechanism_review.summary: A college game margin is a sum of possession-level scoring differences, so the expected margin is the tempo-scaled gap between two opponent-adjusted efficiency ratings plus a venue term, and the margin sd scales with the square root of possessions (roughly 10 to 11 points for a typical game, wider when tempo is high or three-point reliance is large). The mean is poorly known: rosters turn over heavily through the transfer portal, so early-season ratings are priors with large posterior sd, and who actually plays (often undisclosed) shifts the mean by points. Around the mean the realised margin is not a clean Gaussian: favourites in lopsided games pull starters and let leads erode (compressing spread covers for big favourites), and trailing teams foul late (inflating the favourite's final margin by free throws while leaving winner probability unchanged), so winner, cover, bucket and parlay contracts read different parts of one mixture-shaped distribution.

stages.name: Latent strength gap with roster-churn prior
stages.description: Each side has a latent per-possession strength (offense minus defense, opponent-adjusted) that must be estimated from a thin schedule: about 30 games, a connected graph only through conference play, and heavy roster turnover through the transfer portal. Early in the season the preseason prior (returning minutes, portal arrivals, recruiting, coach) carries most weight; by January the in-season ratings dominate. The gap is a posterior, not a point, and its sd is largest for new-roster teams and for isolated schedules. Two cases fall outside D1 ratings: a D1 team facing a lower-division or reclassifying opponent needs a tier prior, and KXNCAAMBD3GAME pairs two Division III teams, whose gap must come from a separate D3 rating fitted on D3 results only (the D3 graph connects to D1 through very few games).
stages.distribution: Gaussian posterior on the rating gap with sd shrinking roughly like 1/sqrt(games played); heavy-tailed for new rosters and for opponents with fewer than a handful of D1 games.

stages.name: Who actually plays tonight
stages.description: The strength gap is conditional on the active rotation. College programs have no mandated injury report, so a star's status is often revealed minutes before tip through starters lists or warm-up news, and the market may price the scratch before a pregame feed does. The effect of an absence depends on replacement quality and bench depth: with a seven-man rotation a missing starter costs more than in a ten-man one. The model must treat status as a probability mixture over scenarios rather than as a label.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over rotation scenarios (starter in/out, minutes-limited), each shifting the mean by roughly 0 to 6 points; probabilities of each scenario are themselves uncertain and time-dependent.

stages.name: Venue, travel and schedule-spot shift
stages.description: Home court adds a mean shift of about three to four points on average but varies by arena, crowd and altitude, and collapses toward zero or reverses on neutral floors (in-season events, conference tournaments, the Crown). Rest, travel and third-games-in-days effects are small in college but matter in multi-game events. Schedule spots (buy games, rivalry, post-exam lull, lookahead to conference play) change effort and rotation, which feeds the blowout stage as much as the mean.
stages.distribution: Approximately constant shift per venue class with team-specific deviations that need heavy shrinkage (team home edge is noisy over about 15 home games); schedule-spot effects are small and unevenly measurable.

stages.name: Possession count and margin variance
stages.description: Final margin variance is not a constant: it grows with the number of possessions and with three-point reliance (three-point shooting is a high-variance way to score). The slower side often controls tempo, so a low-possession game with an underdog that shoots many threes widens the effective upset probability beyond what the same mean gap gives in a fast game. Expected possession count is a negotiated quantity from both teams' adjusted tempo.
stages.distribution: Margin sd scales approximately with sqrt(possessions) times a shot-profile factor; tempo itself has about 3 to 4 possession residual sd; pace control is asymmetric (slow team usually wins the argument).

stages.name: Late-game script and blowout compression
stages.description: Observed margin differs from the in-game 'true' margin through two end-of-game mechanisms. In a lopsided game the favourite's coach substitutes freely, so the lead decays or stalls; whether a 25-point halftime lead ends at 18 or 30 depends heavily on the coach's bench-clearing habit and on the opponent's garbage-time scoring. In a close game the trailing team fouls and the leader's free-throw conversion extends or protects the margin without changing who wins. Overtime converts a tied game into a 1 to 6 point margin. The catalog definitions of cbb.blowout_garbage (P(|margin|>15) by spread), cbb.ot_model (OT frequency by closing spread) and cbb.late_game_foul_script (cover flips versus spread) are conditioned here on the fundamentals expected margin, never on the market spread.
stages.distribution: Regime mixture: competitive regime (margin approximately normal) and blowout regime (compressed with a coach-specific decay), with overtime adding a spike of 1 to 6 point margins; the mixture weight is a threshold-like function of the expected margin.

stages.name: Contract mapping and joint outcomes
stages.description: The same margin distribution settles different contracts. Moneyline reads P(margin > 0), spread reads a tail at a .5 strike, winning margin reads a bucket pmf, and the same-game parlay needs the joint of margin and total because favourites in blowouts both cover and (through starters resting) tend to push totals under or over depending on tempo. Settlement frictions (a game not started within 48 hours for the D1 series, or not rescheduled within two weeks for KXNCAAMBD3GAME, resolves to a fair price; official score vs a later correction) censor or relabel rows.
stages.distribution: Discrete integer margin with a continuous latent; correlation between margin and total is weakly positive for fast favourites and negative when a blowout slows scoring; void probability is small but nonzero (a few percent in early-season weather or cancellation windows).

contract_review.settlement_definition: YES settles on the official result of one named game: the named team wins outright (KXNCAAMBGAME for Division I games; KXNCAAMBD3GAME for Division III games such as the DIII championship, where both teams are Division III), wins by more than a .5 floor_strike (KXNCAAMBSPREAD, no push), wins by a stated integer bucket such as 6 to 10 (KXNCAAMBWINMARGIN), or satisfies a conjunction of a spread cover and a total under (KXNCAAMBSGP). The game is identified by teams and original scheduled date. D1 series: a postponement that tips within 48 hours stays open and settles on the official final result; a game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves to a fair price. KXNCAAMBD3GAME instead stays open for a rescheduled game within two weeks and otherwise resolves to a fair price for each team. The winner series imply overtime is played to a result; the spread, margin and parlay text never states whether overtime points count.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final score as published for the game (NCAA/ESPN box score); the sampled rules cite 'the official final result' without naming a provider, so provider hierarchy on score corrections is unverified.
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime: the winner series (GAME, D3GAME) name only the team that wins, which implies the result after overtime; the spread, winning-margin and parlay rules say 'official final result' (spread, margin) or nothing (parlay) and never state whether OT points count toward the margin. A five-minute OT collapses most close games to a 1-to-6 point margin.
Strikes end in .5 so there is no push; WINMARGIN buckets (for example 6 to 10) have integer edges so a margin of exactly 5 or 11 falls in a neighbour bucket.

Delay windows differ: D1 series (GAME, SPREAD, WINMARGIN) stay open for a game that begins within 48 hours and otherwise resolve to a fair price; KXNCAAMBD3GAME stays open for up to two weeks. The sampled KXNCAAMBSGP text has no postponement clause at all.

KXNCAAMBD3GAME is Division III versus Division III (the sampled market is the DIII national championship game); neither team has a D1 adjusted-efficiency rating, so the strength gap must come from a Division III rating built from D3 results.

Extreme rungs (a 50.5-point strike for Oklahoma St. against Queens) sit in the blowout regime: whether they hit depends on bench-clearing and garbage-time scoring more than on the efficiency gap, and the underdog's rating may rest on few D1 seasons.
Postponement within the window keeps the market open but moves tip time, so lineup news and rest assumptions made at open can be stale.

game_total.label: CBB full-game total points

game_total.mechanism: Total = expected possessions x combined efficiency. Tempo is negotiated and the slower side often controls it; efficiency depends on opponent-adjusted offense/defense with luck regression on three-point shooting; FT rate and late-game fouling add points; thin disclosure of injuries shifts pace and efficiency. Sharp totals are good, so edges come from availability mixtures, shooting-luck regression and rung-level mispricing.

interactions.hypothesis: Strong-defense, slow teams cut totals non-additively because tempo control and half-court defense compound.
Offenses boosted by recent hot three-point shooting are overrated for totals; regress by 3PA share.
Whistle-heavy games lengthen games and add FT points when teams are good FT shooters.
A missing primary ball handler slows tempo and lowers transition scoring, interacting with the efficiency loss.
Close-game late fouling raises totals; the effect is concentrated in games with small spreads.

A strong half-court defence that forces long possessions lowers both the number of possessions and points per possession, so the effect on the total is the product of the two reductions, larger than the sum of separate tempo and defence effects, in slow-tempo teams in particular.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress total residual on tempo, adjusted defence and their product using prior seasons; check whether the interaction coefficient is negative for slow-and-strong-defence matchups.

interactions.hypothesis: Recent shooting above expectation is regressed toward shot-quality expectation with weight depending on the attempt share: a team with 45 percent of shots from three has far more luck-driven variance, so its recent over-performance should be discounted harder than a rim-based team's.
interactions.how_to_test: Split teams by 3PA share and compare how well last-8-games 3P% minus season mean predicts the next game's offensive efficiency, expecting a higher regression slope for high-share teams.

interactions.hypothesis: Extra fouls add points only through free-throw conversion, so the whistle effect on the total is foul count times combined free-throw percentage; a whistle-heavy crew with two poor free-throw teams adds much less than the same crew with two 78 percent teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute predicted FT points = expected FTA (crew and teams) x team FT% and test its incremental coefficient in a total residual regression versus separate linear terms.

interactions.hypothesis: Intentional fouling adds points only if the game is within roughly 8 points with under two minutes left, so the add-on is a step function of projected closeness; in games decided earlier it contributes nothing and the bench-clearing effect pushes the total down. Closeness is the model's competitive-regime probability, not a market spread.
interactions.how_to_test: Bucket games by absolute margin at the 2:00 mark and compare points scored in the last two minutes; confirm the jump happens inside the 8-point band.

interactions.hypothesis: The pace effect of an injury exists only if the missing player is one of the team's primary ball handlers, and its sign differs from a rim-protector absence, so the injury input must be mapped to a role before it can shift the total.
interactions.how_to_test: Using games with a missing starter, compare changes in possessions per 40 by player role (handler vs big) against the team's season average.

nonlinearities.shape: step addition of roughly 15 to 18 combined points (pace arithmetic, to be measured) with probability 5 to 6 percent (assumed base rate, to be measured); right skew
nonlinearities.why: Overtime is a mixture component: it shifts the upper tail of the total by a block of points rather than adding a small smooth amount, which matters for high strikes where the OT bump can flip the result.

nonlinearities.shape: approximately linear in possessions but convex in the combined slow-slow region because shot-clock violations and long possessions hold scoring down
nonlinearities.why: When both teams are in the slowest tail of tempo, each possession tends to end later in the shot clock, lowering per-possession efficiency, so total falls faster than a linear mapping from possessions suggests.

nonlinearities.shape: variance of total increases convexly with combined three-point attempt share
nonlinearities.why: Each additional three-point attempt replaces a lower-variance two or free-throw attempt, so total sd grows faster than the mean when both teams shoot many threes, shifting probability into both tails of the strike ladder.

mechanism_review.summary: Total points are possessions times combined points per possession plus an overtime tail. Possessions come from a negotiation of two adjusted tempos moderated by average possession length, shot-clock violations and turnover or foul stoppages; per-possession scoring comes from opponent-adjusted offense versus defense, shot profile (three-point share and rim rate) and free-throw production, with a large luck component in shooting that mean-reverts. The result is a roughly normal distribution with an sd near 11 to 12 points, plus a right tail created by overtime (about 5 to 6 percent (assumed base rate, to be measured) of games, adding roughly 15 to 18 combined points by pace arithmetic, to be measured) and late-game intentional fouling in close games, and a left tail created by blowouts with bench play and by teams that slow a game when ahead. Availability changes tempo as well as efficiency (a missing lead guard usually lowers possessions), and the league-wide scoring baseline drifts across a season and across rule-emphasis years.

stages.name: Possession count from two tempos
stages.description: Expected possessions are not the average of two adjusted tempos: each side's average possession length, its transition share and how long it works the shot clock decide how much of the 40 minutes becomes possessions, and the defence that forces long possessions stretches the count. Turnover rate and the number of whistles (each foul stops the clock and ends a possession) subtract or add possessions. The slower team usually controls the pace, so an interaction of the two tempos is needed rather than a mean.
stages.distribution: Possession count approximately normal around 65 to 72 with a game-level sd near 3 to 4; the pace-control asymmetry skews the realised count toward the slower team's preference.

stages.name: Points per possession from two adjusted units
stages.description: Each team's expected points per possession is its opponent-adjusted offence against the other side's adjusted defence, modified by shot profile (rim, mid-range, three share) and the four factors (shooting, turnovers, offensive rebounding, free throws). A large share of recent shooting results is luck: three-point and free-throw percentages regress hard to shot quality and to talent, particularly for teams with a high three-point attempt share. League-wide scoring level also drifts through the season and with rule emphasis, so the baseline must move with a short half-life.
stages.distribution: Per-possession points approximately normal with a game-level sd that depends on shot mix; three-point-heavy games have visibly wider sd than rim-and-free-throw games.

stages.name: Whistle and free-throw production
stages.description: Foul and free-throw volume is set by the crew's calls per game, the teams' foul-drawing and foul-committing rates, and the bonus structure (1-and-1 at the 7th team foul in a half, two shots from the 10th). Free throws are points without clock time, so a high-foul game both lengthens the game and lifts efficiency, in proportion to the teams' free-throw percentage. The crew is often assigned late and unannounced, which limits how much can be used pregame.
stages.distribution: Free-throw attempts per game are overdispersed (sd about 6 to 7 around a mean near 35 combined), and the crew effect is a few points of total per game at most.

stages.name: Personnel and rotation effects on both inputs
stages.description: A missing creator reduces possessions and transition scoring at the same time and usually costs the offence more than the defence; a missing rim protector raises opponent efficiency without affecting tempo. Because injury news in college is thin, the realised lineup is a mixture and the total's mean inherits that mixture. Rest and travel add small fatigue effects mainly in multi-game events.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over scenarios (key creator or rim protector in or out) with combined mean shifts of about 1 to 5 points of total.

stages.name: Late-game script and overtime tail
stages.description: Close games end with deliberate fouling by the trailing team, which converts each remaining possession into one or two free throws and adds points, while a blowout reduces efficiency through bench units and often shortens possessions. A tie at the end of regulation adds five minutes of extra play, roughly 15 to 18 combined points by pace arithmetic (about 8 to 9 possessions per team in five minutes at about 1 point per possession; to be measured) and rarely a second or third extra period. These two end-of-game mechanisms create a right tail and a left tail that a symmetric distribution around the mean misses. Whether the late-foul add-on applies depends on the model's probability that the game is in the competitive regime (cbb.margin_regime_mixture), not on the market spread.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed mixture: normal body, overtime spike (about +15 to +18 combined, to be measured) with probability near 5 to 6 percent (assumed base rate, to be measured), and a late-fouling add of a few points concentrated in games within five points at the two-minute mark.

stages.name: Contract mapping: nested total strikes
stages.description: Each over strike reads the upper tail of one combined-points distribution, and the rungs listed for one game are nested events whose probabilities must fall monotonically as the strike rises; rungs far from the median (the sample lists 126.5 for a Kansas home game) are dominated by the shape of the tails, i.e. the overtime mixture and the late-foul add-on, rather than by the mean. Settlement frictions (overtime inclusion not stated, the 48-hour void window resolving to a fair price) change or censor the label.
stages.distribution: Integer combined points with a smooth body and an overtime bump in the right tail; rung probabilities are a monotone decreasing step function of the strike.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXNCAAMBTOTAL settles YES when the combined points of both teams in the named game exceed the half-point floor_strike ('over 126.5 total points are scored'), so no push. The game is identified by teams and original scheduled date; a postponement that tips within 48 hours stays open and resolves on the official final result, and a game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves to a fair price. The rules do not say whether overtime points are included in the total, only that it resolves on the official final result.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final result of the game as stated in the rules ('official final result'); no named provider (NCAA, ESPN or school sites) in the sampled text.
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime inclusion in the points total is not spelled out in the sampled TOTAL rules (compare 2H markets which explicitly say inclusive of overtime); the total strike therefore has an unverified OT component worth roughly 15 to 18 combined points by pace arithmetic (unmeasured, see tot_base_rates) in the 5 to 6 percent (assumed base rate, to be measured) of games that go to extra time.
Strikes ending in .5 mean no push; adjacent rungs of the same game (for example 126.5 and 127.5) are nested events with a monotone probability curve.
A game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves to a fair price rather than NO, so early-season weather or arena issues create censored labels.
Only one live series (KXNCAAMBTOTAL) remains; the overtime probability is still needed here as the right-tail component of the total, not as a settled event of its own.

team_total.target: One named team's points over a half-point strike (OT per rules text)
team_total.mechanism: Team points = own possessions x own efficiency against the opponent's defense, correlated with margin: favorites' bench minutes in blowouts and underdogs' late free throws shape the team distribution. Team total, game total and spread markets must be coherent; mismatches signal edges. Availability of the team's scorers and the opponent's rim protection move the team total directly.

interactions.hypothesis: Favorite team total is shaded down and underdog up by blowout/late-foul dynamics compared with a linear split.
Offensive efficiency against zone/press differs from average defense; style matchups alter team points.
Own ball-handler absence changes both pace and efficiency of the team.

In competitive games a team's points rise roughly half-for-half with the margin, but once the expected margin passes about 15 the favourite's points stop rising (starters sit, possessions shorten) while the underdog's points are propped up by late fouls, so the slope flips between regimes.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the slope of points on margin separately for expected-margin buckets and favourite/underdog roles; test for a slope break near 15 points.

interactions.hypothesis: A three-point-reliant offence loses efficiency against a pack-line or rim-focused man defence but gains against a zone that concedes threes; the team's baseline offence is therefore conditional on the opposing scheme, and the sign of the style effect flips with the team's shot profile.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress points per possession on offence rating, opponent scheme dummy and the team's three-point share times the scheme dummy using games in which the opponent's scheme is recorded.

interactions.hypothesis: When a slow-tempo team meets a fast team, whose pace wins depends on each team's elasticity: scoring volume equals the elasticity-weighted tempo times points per possession, so a team that dictates pace adds or removes points for the opponent too.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predicted possessions from average of tempos versus elasticity-weighted tempos against realised possessions in games with extreme tempo gaps.

interactions.hypothesis: The favourite's total beyond the starters' minutes is the product of the probability of a blowout and the bench unit's scoring rate in that scenario; both are uncertain and positively linked to coach style, so they should be modelled jointly instead of averaged.
interactions.how_to_test: Use games with leads of 15 plus; compute points per possession of non-starters by coach and test if blowout probability and bench efficiency covary across teams.

interactions.hypothesis: A team's free-throw points are its drawing rate times the opponent's foul propensity times conversion; a rim-attacking team against a foul-prone defence has a larger amplification than either factor suggests alone, in close games late in the half when the bonus applies.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress team FTA on own FT rate, opponent allowed FT rate and their product, and compare to an additive specification.

interactions.hypothesis: Because the contract pays only the single highest score, a team's chance rises convexly with its expected possessions relative to the other teams in the round: a few extra possessions move a fast team from near the top to the top far more often than they lift a slow team, and the effect grows with the number of games in the round.
interactions.how_to_test: In historical rounds, regress the indicator of holding the round maximum on team tempo rank within the round, controlling for expected team total; look for curvature at the top tempo ranks.

nonlinearities.shape: concave saturation of the favourite's points in expected margin, with a flat segment beyond a lead of about 20
nonlinearities.why: As the favourite's lead grows, starters sit and the clock matters less, so team points stop growing and then fall relative to a linear projection; this makes high team-total strikes for big favourites systematically less likely than a total-less-spread split implies.

nonlinearities.shape: regression weight increasing in three-point attempt share and decreasing in games played (hyperbolic shrinkage)
nonlinearities.why: Shooting luck in a team total has an sd of roughly 8 to 9 points; the right amount of regression depends on how many three-point attempts underpin the observed percentage, a non-linear shrinkage rather than a fixed rate.

nonlinearities.shape: convex penalty to the opponent's scoring against elite rim protection and to the named team's three-point rate
nonlinearities.why: The effect of a very strong defence on one team's points is larger than linear because elite defences remove the highest-value shots (rim and open threes) and force low-value late-clock shots.

mechanism_review.summary: One team's points are the game's possession count (shared with the opponent, so differing by at most one) times that team's points per possession, plus overtime points. The possession count is a negotiation of both tempos, but the team's own scoring rate depends on its offence versus the opponent's defence, its shot profile against that defence's scheme (zone, press, rim protection), free-throw production against the opponent's foul propensity, and the shooting luck component that regresses. Unlike the game total, a team total is coupled to the margin: a favourite's points saturate once its starters sit in a blowout and the opponent's bench and late-fouling free throws then decide how many points the underdog gets, so one team's distribution is shifted and skewed by its role in the game script.

stages.name: Shared possession count and team pace control
stages.description: Both teams have almost exactly the same number of possessions, so a team cannot buy extra scoring chances alone; its own points depend on the game's tempo, which is set by whichever team imposes its preferred pace. Some teams are elastic (they speed up against a fast opponent), others dictate regardless; this elasticity matters because a pace-setting team facing a slower opponent gets fewer possessions than its adjusted tempo implies, and the market may assume the average of tempos.
stages.distribution: Possessions approximately normal with sd 3 to 4, shared by both teams; team-specific elasticity to opponent pace ranges from near zero (pace dictators) to near one (pace adapters).

stages.name: Own points per possession against this defence
stages.description: A team's expected points per possession is its adjusted offence against the specific defence it faces, adjusted for shot profile (a rim-attacking team against a shot-blocking centre, a three-point-heavy team against a zone that gives threes), turnover pressure from presses, and the four factors. Scoring luck is large in a 30-game sample, so recent three-point hot streaks are regressed toward shot-quality expectation, with the regression stronger for teams that shoot many threes.
stages.distribution: Per-possession scoring approximately normal for one team with game-level sd about 8 to 9 points of team total from shooting variance, and a mean that depends on the scheme interaction.

stages.name: Free-throw production against the foul profile
stages.description: Free throws are points that cost no clock. How many a team gets depends on how it attacks (rim and post trips draw fouls) and on how many fouls the opponent commits per possession; the bonus rules (1-and-1 at the 7th team foul in a half, two shots from the 10th) raise the yield of every late-half foul. Conversion depends on the team's free-throw percentage with a regression toward talent in small samples.
stages.distribution: Free-throw attempts for one team are overdispersed (sd about 5 around a mean near 18 to 20), and FT% for one game has an sd near 10 percentage points.

stages.name: Scoring role in the game script (favourite versus underdog)
stages.description: A team total is coupled to the margin in an asymmetric way. A heavy favourite scores above its base until the lead is large, then its starters sit and its per-possession scoring and pace fall, capping its total; an underdog's total is lifted by its own pace but is shaped by garbage-time bench play and late fouling free throws when trailing. The bench unit's efficiency, rather than the starters', governs how many points a team scores in the final minutes of a lopsided game. Blowout and late-foul terms are keyed to the fundamentals expected margin used in cbb.team_points_margin_coupling, not to the market spread or to cbb.implied_team_totals.
stages.distribution: Role-dependent skew: favourite's team total is capped (left-skewed beyond a lead threshold), underdog's is right-skewed through late free throws; the coupling slope to margin is near 0.5 in the competitive zone and falls toward 0.2 in blowouts.

stages.name: Availability of own scorers and opposing defenders
stages.description: Because the contract reads one team's points, the injury effect is directional: a scorer missing for the named team lowers its total, while a missing rim protector on the opponent raises it. Disclosure is thin in college, so the mean is a mixture over scenarios. Replacement quality and the usage redistribution to remaining players determine the net loss, since part of a missing scorer's shots go to teammates at lower efficiency.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over own-scorer and opponent-defender scenarios, shifting the team total by roughly 2 to 6 points when a lead scorer is out.

stages.name: Overtime and contract mapping
stages.description: An overtime period adds roughly 7 to 9 points to each team's score (pace arithmetic, unmeasured), so the ladder's upper rungs include an OT mixture component. Adjacent rungs of one team's ladder are nested, and the two teams' ladders in the same game are jointly constrained by the game total and spread (home plus away points equals the total), so a consistent set of team totals needs a joint model, not two independent ones.
stages.distribution: Mixture with a small overtime component (5 to 6 percent of games, +7 to +9 points per team) and strong dependence between the two sides' scores through the shared possession count.

stages.name: Round maximum across simultaneous tournament games
stages.description: For KXNCAAMBTEAMMOSTPTS the object is the largest team score among all teams in one tournament round. Each game contributes two coupled team scores (shared possessions, margin coupling); across games the scores are close to independent apart from a shared tournament-wide scoring level (neutral arenas, dome sightlines for Final Four venues). The maximum is pulled toward high-tempo, efficient offences, toward games whose expected total is high, and toward games with an overtime chance; a slow elite team can have a high win probability yet a small most-points probability. Before the round's teams are known, the probability also integrates over who advances, from the bracket simulation.
stages.distribution: Maximum of 2G correlated integer team scores (G games): right-skewed order statistic with an integer pmf and a non-trivial tie mass at the top; Monte Carlo over the joint team-score model.

talent_strength.note: Own offence against opponent defence; the opponent's adjusted defence is the stronger single predictor of the named team's points. The fundamentals-only rating, preseason prior and its posterior sd are included because early-season team totals rest on the prior (roster churn) and the width of the ladder depends on rating uncertainty.

pace_volume.note: The count is shared between teams; own tempo alone mislabels the driver.

distribution_variance.note: Skewness differs by role in the game; sd of one team's points is about 8 to 9 points.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and travel move both teams' efficiency by a fraction of a point per 100 possessions, far below the 8 to 9 point sd of one team's score, and no stable team-specific effect has been shown in college data.

officiating_rules.note: Whistle tendency changes free-throw yield for the team; the catalog input exists but was not attached to this archetype.

settlement_contract.note: Strike construction, void rule and OT treatment inferred; a monotone ladder per team and consistency with the game total.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Two series. KXNCAAMBTEAMTOTAL settles YES when the named team's own points in the identified game exceed the .5 floor_strike (no push); a postponement that tips within 48 hours stays open and settles on the official final result, and a game cancelled or not started within 48 hours resolves to a fair price; overtime inclusion is not stated. KXNCAAMBTEAMMOSTPTS settles YES if the named team scores the most points of any team in a named round of the men's tournament (sampled: the Semifinals of the 2026 tournament); if N teams tie for the most, YES pays $1/N rounded down to the cent. Its text states no overtime, postponement or forfeit rule.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official final result of the game; no provider named in the sampled text.
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime inclusion in a team's points is not stated in the sampled rules; the official final score would include it, adding roughly 7 to 9 points to each team (half of the 15 to 18 combined points of pace arithmetic, unmeasured) in the roughly 5 to 6 percent of games that go to extra time.
The sampled strike (89.5 for a team in a game with a presumably high total) shows team-total rungs sit well above typical team scores, so the market spans a wide tail rather than only the median.
Neutral-site or tournament games name teams by listing order, so the home/away label cannot be relied on to identify the venue effect.

KXNCAAMBTEAMMOSTPTS compares teams across different games of a round (two games and four teams in the Semifinals; up to 32 games in the Round of 64), so it rewards fast, high-scoring teams and teams whose games may go to overtime, and requires the joint of all team scores in the round.
Ties for the round maximum pay $1/N rounded down to the cent; whether overtime points count and what happens if a game in the round is forfeited or not played are not stated in the most-points text.

first_half.label: CBB first-half winner, spread and total
first_half.target: First-half winner, margin or total over a strike (halves; OT excluded unless stated)
first_half.mechanism: First-half scoring is driven by starters and tempo, the first-half share of game scoring (team-specific), early foul trouble, and half-end bonus dynamics. Game-level markets are better priced than half-level derivatives, so inconsistencies between half and game lines are a source of edge; ties in half winners matter.

Gives a half-specific possession count for 1H total and spread rungs that existing tempo (game level) does not.
Converts foul risk into expected first-half starter minutes, the biggest first-half-specific variance source.
