contract_review.settlement_definition: Eleven outright series. National title: KXMARMAD (YES if the named team is the Division 1 Men's National Champion); which conference supplies the champion: KXNCAAMBCONF (affiliation as recognised by the NCAA when the tournament begins, with an 'Other' bucket) and KXMARMADCONFWIN (same object, no affiliation rule stated); KXNCAAMB2ML, a conjunction of a named men's champion and a named women's champion. Other brackets: KXNCAAMBNIT (NIT champion), KXNCAAMBCBC (College Basketball Crown winner), KXNCAAMBTOURNEY (an early-season multi-team event, sampled as the 2026 Players Era 8). Title-only listings with no rules text: KXMARMADREGION (region winner), KXNCAAMBHL and KXNCAAMBSUN (Horizon and Atlantic Sun tournament winners) and KXNCAAMBBIG10REG (Big Ten regular-season champion). Each settles on the organising body's result; no sampled text addresses vacated titles, ineligibility or a cancelled event.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: The governing bodies' official results (NCAA for the national championship, each conference for its tournament and standings); the sampled rules name no URL or provider.
variants_and_edge_cases: Objects differ inside the archetype: six-win national title (KXMARMAD), sums of title probability over a conference (KXNCAAMBCONF, KXMARMADCONFWIN), a product across the men's and women's tournaments (KXNCAAMB2ML), the NIT and Crown (fields of teams NOT in the NCAA bracket), and a November in-season event (KXNCAAMBTOURNEY).

KXNCAAMBCONF defines affiliation at the start of the NCAA tournament and an 'Other' bucket for every team outside the Big East, Big Ten, Big 12, ACC and SEC, independents included; KXMARMADCONFWIN states no affiliation rule, so the two listings of one object may settle differently for a realigning team.

KXNCAAMB2ML requires both the named men's and the named women's champion; the two events share no games, so the joint is close to the product of marginals, but the women's marginal needs its own ratings and bracket.
NIT and Crown winners must first NOT be selected for the NCAA field and then be invited and accept, so their probability is non-monotone in strength (the best teams are in the NCAA field).

KXNCAAMBTOURNEY: the sampled event (Players Era 8) is a fixed invited field at one neutral venue over a few days; format (pool play versus bracket, tiebreak by point differential) decides who reaches the final and is not stated in the rules.
Vacated titles, postseason bans, ineligible teams and a cancelled event are not addressed in any sampled text.

KXMARMADREGION, KXNCAAMBHL, KXNCAAMBSUN and KXNCAAMBBIG10REG have no listing or rules text; KXNCAAMBHL and KXNCAAMBSUN appear to duplicate KXNCAAMBHOR and KXNCAAMBASUN (filed in futures_conference), and BIG10REG duplicates KXNCAAMBBIGTENREG, whose rules pay 1/N to co-champions.

interactions.hypothesis: Equal-rated teams differ in title odds by remaining schedule and tiebreaker exposure.
Multi-day tournaments compress rest and raise variance; deep, experienced rotations are favored.
Teams needing the auto-bid play with higher intensity than comfortable at-large teams.

The value of a double bye depends on how much better the bye team is than the field: for a dominant team the bye removes two games it would usually win and adds little, while for a top seed only slightly better than seeds 3 to 6 the bye removes two coin-flip-adjacent games and can raise title probability by a third.
interactions.how_to_test: In simulations and in past conference tournaments, compare title rates of bye and non-bye teams across bins of rating gap to the next-best team.

interactions.hypothesis: Probability of a top-4 finish depends on the distribution of the fourth-best win total in the whole league, which changes with how many strong teams there are; the same team has a lower probability in a league with six contenders than in one with four, and the tie-inclusive rule raises it most when the cutoff is crowded.
interactions.how_to_test: Evaluate the same team's top-4 probability across simulated league compositions and compare tie-inclusive and tiebreaker-based ranks.

interactions.hypothesis: The expected share depends on the joint distribution of the top contenders' records, not on each marginal: two equal contenders who rarely lose outside their head-to-head games tie often, halving each share, whereas the same marginals with independent loss patterns produce more sole titles.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare expected shares from the joint simulation with those from independent per-team record distributions holding marginals fixed; check against historical co-champion frequencies by league.

interactions.hypothesis: Effort changes appear only after a team's stakes cross a threshold: a team that clinched the top seed loses incentive and may rest starters in the final games, while a team one win away from a double bye does not; the effect is a function of leverage computed from the standings simulation.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare late-season margin residuals for teams with clinched status versus similar teams with high leverage, using the simulation-based leverage measure.

interactions.hypothesis: Seeding ties matter only when they straddle a bye line or a bracket-side boundary; within a seed band they change nothing, but a two-way tie for the last double bye moves one team's path from three wins to four, a discrete jump in championship-game probability.
interactions.how_to_test: In simulated seasons, measure the change in QUAL probability for teams whose tie status crosses a bye line versus teams tied within a band.

nonlinearities.shape: convex mapping from team strength to conference tournament title probability
nonlinearities.why: Title needs three or four consecutive wins, so the probability is roughly the product of per-game probabilities; a one-point rating edge compounds across rounds and the mapping steepens for teams near the top of the league.

nonlinearities.shape: step-like share: 1, 1/2, 1/3 as tie count rises
nonlinearities.why: The payout falls in discrete steps with the number of tied teams, so a small change in the probability of a two-way tie can move the expected share far more than the same change in the probability of the best record.

nonlinearities.shape: cutoff crowding effect: top-N probability rises with tie mass at the cutoff
nonlinearities.why: Because tied teams all count, the effective probability of a team at the margin of the top four increases non-linearly with the share of simulations in which three or more teams tie at the fourth-place win total.

mechanism_review.summary: These contracts are functions of one conference season and its postseason tournament. Regular-season series are statistics of the joint distribution of all members' conference records: the top-N series is an order statistic with tie-inclusive settlement, and the champion series pays a share 1/N that depends on how many teams tie for first, so the number of ties is itself the target. Conference records come from 18 to 20 conference games per team on unbalanced schedules (some opponents once, some twice, venue alternating) whose win probabilities share each team's uncertain latent strength, which correlates a team's results and makes members' records negatively dependent (one team's win is another's loss). Tournament and championship-game series then run a short single-elimination bracket seeded from those standings with the league's own tiebreaks, byes and sites, so path length and hosting can matter as much as rating.

stages.name: Season-long strength as a shared latent variable
stages.description: Every conference game a team plays draws on the same underlying strength, uncertain at pricing time; if the team is better than its rating, most of its 18 to 20 league games are easier than priced. The uncertainty is larger for rosters with heavy transfer turnover and shrinks as league play progresses, but never to zero. This shared factor fattens the tails of a team's conference record, which drives the chance of a sole title, a share of first and a top-seed bye in the conference tournament.
stages.distribution: Normal posterior on team strength with sd about 2 to 3 points of adjusted margin early in the season, decaying with games played; the shared factor induces a game-to-game correlation of about 0.05 to 0.15 in outcomes.

stages.name: Which games count: the conference schedule
stages.description: Standings are built only from conference games: 18 to 20 per team, with post-realignment leagues of 16 to 18 members playing unbalanced schedules in which some opponents appear once and some twice, home or away. Which repeat opponents a team draws, and where, shifts its expected conference record by up to a win in strong leagues. Non-conference games, exempt events and postseason play do not count for these series; a cancelled league game that is not made up leaves teams with unequal game counts.
stages.distribution: Fixed discrete schedule known before the season: 18 to 20 conference games per team, home share near one half, with team-specific repeat-opponent strength.

stages.name: Game-level win probabilities with venue and availability
stages.description: Each conference game's win probability comes from the strength gap plus a venue shift (home or away; conference tournament games at neutral or campus sites), rest and a minutes-weighted availability adjustment for known absences. Road games against the top third of a league are where contenders drop the losses that decide first place, so the venue term and the draw of road opponents are central to who finishes first.
stages.distribution: Probit link with game sd near 10.5 points; conference-game win probability ranges from about 10 percent (road at the league's best) to about 95 percent (home against the worst member).

stages.name: Regular-season champion: how many share first
stages.description: A regular-season champion series pays 1 to a sole declared champion and 1/N to each of N declared co-champions, so the quantity priced is the expected share, not the probability of holding the best record. Leagues with several near-equal contenders produce two-way and three-way ties for first in a substantial share of seasons, and each tie cuts a share; whether the league declares co-champions or names one through tiebreakers then decides the payout. The standings simulation must keep ties unbroken for this series.
stages.distribution: Discrete distribution of the number of teams tied at the top (1, 2, 3 or more) from the joint conference records; expected share is a mixture over that count.

stages.name: Conference order statistics with tie-inclusive cutoffs
stages.description: A top-N conference finish is determined by the N-th best conference record among all members, and each team that ties at or above that record counts. Because conference games are zero-sum, members' records are negatively dependent and independent per-team models fail; tiebreakers, used for tournament seeding, are not used for this settlement. The cutoff depth differs by series (top 2 for the Big 12, top 4 elsewhere).
stages.distribution: Joint distribution of conference records with a zero-sum constraint; tie mass at the cutoff is typically 15 to 35 percent in 14 to 18 team leagues.

stages.name: Conference tournament: seeding, byes, sites and the path to the final
stages.description: Tournament and championship-game series run a short single-elimination bracket seeded from the final standings using the league's own tiebreak procedure. Top seeds often receive double byes (two fewer wins needed), some one-bid leagues host early rounds on the higher seed's campus, and the Ivy League takes only four teams. A team reaches the final by winning two to four games and the title with one more, on consecutive days in most leagues. Reaching the final also depends on which side of the bracket the strongest rival lands, which follows from seeding ties.
stages.distribution: Per-team title probability from a 2-to-5-round bracket; top-seed title probability typically 25 to 45 percent and championship-game probability roughly 45 to 65 percent in 12-to-16-team leagues.

talent_strength.note: Shared latent strength with uncertainty is the foundation for season-long events.

opponent_matchup.note: Game-level matchup variance and the conference tournament bracket structure.

role_personnel.note: Availability-adjusted rating captures who plays, but roster role detail is secondary for season-long events.

availability_news.note: Injuries enter through the strength posterior and game-level adjustment; a long absence of a star changes the shared factor for the rest of the season.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching effects on conference records and tournament runs are captured by team ratings; no coach-level driver separate from rating is established, and late-season rest after clinching is covered by the clinch input.

environment.note: Home and away allocation of conference games and campus versus neutral conference tournament sites.

game_context_script.note: In-game script (blowouts, foul games) changes margins but not whether a team wins or loses, which is what these season-level contracts count; script matters only for spread-like contracts.

pace_volume.note: Possession count affects margin variance within a game, which is reflected in the single-game sd; it is not a separate driver of season win counts or finish ranks.

efficiency_conversion.note: Shooting efficiency luck matters within the ratings pipeline and the shared strength posterior; a separate efficiency input for season-level counts would double count the rating uncertainty.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersed conference records, zero-sum dependence, tie mass at the top and at the top-N cutoff.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Remaining schedule and incentives for teams that clinched or are eliminated late in the season.

officiating_rules.note: Officiating crews rotate across conference games, so no team-specific crew effect changes a conference record or a tournament path beyond what home court and ratings already capture.

settlement_contract.note: Tie-inclusive top-N, 1/N co-champion payout, championship-game qualification and tournament champion; tiebreaks matter for seeding only. Vacated results and bans not addressed.

contract_review.settlement_definition: 52 conference-level series in four templates. (1) Conference tournament champion for about 33 leagues (e.g. KXNCAAMBA10, KXNCAAMBACC, KXNCAAMBSEC; plus alternative listings KXNCAAMBIG12, KXNCAAMBIGEAST, KXNCAAMBIGTEN worded 'wins the Men's ... Basketball Tournament'): YES if the named team is the tournament champion. (2) Championship-game qualifiers (ACCQUAL, BIG12QUAL, BIGEASTQUAL, BIGTENQUAL, SECQUAL): YES if the team qualifies for the conference tournament championship game. (3) Regular-season champion (ACCREG, BIG12REG, BIGEASTREG, BIGTENREG, SECREG): a sole declared champion resolves YES; declared co-champions each resolve at 1/N. (4) Regular-season top-N finish (REGTOP; top 4, top 2 for the Big 12): teams with identical conference win-loss records at the cutoff all count as achieving the position. KXNCAAMBBIG10REGTOP is title only. No text addresses vacated results, postseason bans or a cancelled tournament.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Conference official standings and declared champions (regular-season and REGTOP series) and the conference tournament's official results (champion and championship-game series); the sampled rules name no provider or URL.
variants_and_edge_cases: Top-N finish series (ACC, Big Ten, Big East, SEC top 4; Big 12 top 2) use inclusive ties on conference win-loss records: if three teams tie for 4th, all three resolve YES, so the model computes 'conference record at least the N-th best' rather than rank after tiebreakers.

Regular-season champion series pay 1/N to each declared co-champion; expected payout is the sum over k of P(team shares first with k-1 others)/k, and depends on whether the conference declares co-champions or names one by tiebreaker.

Tournament seeding (and so byes, campus hosting and path length) does use the conference's tiebreak procedure, even though REGTOP settlement does not; the same tie therefore matters for QUAL and tournament series but not for REGTOP.

Duplicate listings: KXNCAAMBIG12/KXNCAAMBBIG12, KXNCAAMBIGEAST/KXNCAAMBBIGEAST and KXNCAAMBIGTEN/KXNCAAMBBIG10 name the same tournaments with two templates; KXNCAAMBBIG10REGTOP (title only) duplicates KXNCAAMBBIGTENREGTOP.

Formats differ by league: four-team Ivy tournament, double byes for top seeds in most high-major leagues, campus-site early rounds in several one-bid leagues, and season labels vary (KXNCAAMBSBELT samples the 2026 tournament).
A team under a postseason ban can win or share a regular-season title but cannot play the tournament; neither case is addressed in the rules.

futures_seed_other.mechanism: Seed and bid outcomes are determined by committee evaluation of resumes (NET, quadrant records, WAB) and predictive metrics, with late results and conference tournaments shifting boundaries; advancement outcomes follow the bracket simulation. Discrete seed boundaries and bid-thief dynamics produce nonlinear probabilities; the consensus of bracketologists is a strong prior.

interactions.hypothesis: Seed outcomes near boundaries depend on late quality wins and committee preferences; model the committee's ranking rather than ratings alone.
Bid-thief probability reduces at-large slots; bubble odds depend jointly on conference tournaments and resume.
Advancement probabilities mix rating-implied and seed-implied base rates; weight by sample size.
Conference strength offsets are uncertain and propagate into SOS and bubble odds.

For teams contending for a one or two seed, predictive ratings and quality wins dominate the committee's ordering, whereas on the bubble the quadrant record and bad losses dominate; the coefficient on predictive ratings relative to resume metrics therefore changes across seed bands.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the ordered probit with interaction terms by seed band and compare out-of-sample log-likelihood to a single-weight model.

interactions.hypothesis: The number of bid thieves depends on the joint outcomes of 30 conference tournaments, so the distribution of at-large slots available to the bubble is a function of the sum of Bernoulli events with unequal probabilities; a single multi-bid league tournament upset can create a thief at once and change the cutoff for all bubble teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate all conference tournaments and compute the distribution of thieves and the bubble cutoff; compare to historical thief counts (0 to 4 per year).

interactions.hypothesis: If the committee weights recent results more, the same cumulative metrics yield different seeds for teams that peaked early versus those that finished strong; the seed distribution is therefore conditional on trajectory in the last month.
interactions.how_to_test: Group teams with equal metric-implied seeds by last-10 trajectory and compare mean seed residuals.

interactions.hypothesis: A bubble team's field probability is near zero or one unless its resume sits within a narrow band around the cutoff; games matter a lot only when the resume is in that band, so the leverage of a game is large near the cutoff and small for locks and for teams far outside.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the change in field probability from a Q1 win versus a Q3 loss for teams at different distances from the cutoff and verify a narrow high-leverage band.

interactions.hypothesis: The seed shift for a missing star depends on how much of the team's rating the player carries; for a team whose value is spread across a deep roster the committee has little reason to move it, while for a one-star team the shift may be larger and uncertain in sign.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress seed residual on the missing player's share of team BPM for teams with a late injury across seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: Upset counts across games in a round are positively correlated through the year's seed-line strength gaps (a weak crop of #2 seeds raises all four 2-15 upset chances together) and negatively linked across rounds (an early upset leaves a weaker team to be upset later or removes an upset chance), so counts are overdispersed relative to independent seed base rates.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the historical variance of round upset counts with the variance implied by independent per-game seed base rates; test whether year-level average rating gap by seed line explains the excess.

interactions.hypothesis: An unbeaten season or a 30-win total needs nearly every game won, so its probability averages a steep product of win probabilities over the strength draw; widening strength uncertainty raises these tail probabilities for top teams above the value at the mean rating.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(undefeated) and P(30+ wins) for top-rated teams with strength sd of 0, 1.5 and 3 points and compare with historical frequencies of unbeaten starts after 10 and 20 games.

interactions.hypothesis: For two named teams to both reach the Round of 16, the seed draw and region placement matter jointly: both being top-4 seeds in different regions makes the joint near the product of marginals, while same-region placement or a possible second-round meeting cuts it sharply.
interactions.how_to_test: In simulations, compare the joint Round-of-16 probability with the product of marginals by region relation (same region, same pod, different region).

nonlinearities.shape: saturating in quality wins (Q1 count) and convex penalty for Q3 and Q4 losses
nonlinearities.why: Additional top-tier wins beyond about six add little to seed, while each additional bad loss costs more than the previous one, so the mapping from record to committee score is neither linear nor symmetric.

nonlinearities.shape: step: each extra bid thief moves the at-large cutoff by exactly one slot
nonlinearities.why: The effective number of at-large slots is an integer function of the thief count, so P(make field) for a bubble team jumps in discrete increments across the thief distribution rather than varying smoothly.

nonlinearities.shape: ordinal step function with fuzzy edges: P(seed line) is bell-shaped in rank with sd 2 to 4 slots
nonlinearities.why: A team ranked 4th or 5th overall has comparable probabilities of being a 1 seed or a 2 seed because of S-curve adjustments; the probability changes sharply across the line boundary rather than linearly with rating.

nonlinearities.shape: extreme-value step: maximum upset margin jumps to 13-15 when any 15/16 seed wins
nonlinearities.why: The biggest-upset statistic is a maximum, so the probability of clearing a high strike is driven almost entirely by the few rare 14-, 15- and 16-seed wins rather than by the typical number of upsets.

mechanism_review.summary: The seed and field are produced by a human committee applying published principles to a set of metrics, so the generating process is a noisy ordinal ranking, not a game outcome. The committee builds a team sheet from result-based measures (NET's team value, quadrant records, wins above bubble, strength of record) and predictive ratings, ranks all candidates, and then fits them into an S-curve with bracketing constraints. The probability a team makes the field is the probability its committee rank lies inside the at-large cutoff after bid thieves (automatic-bid winners who would not have been at-large) are removed; the probability of a given seed line is the probability its slot falls inside a four-slot band after constraint moves. Late results, conference tournaments and committee judgement on injuries and recency add noise, so probabilities near boundaries are sensitive and the entire distribution is step-like (ordinal) rather than smooth. Round-reached outcomes then follow from the bracket simulation conditional on the assigned seed.

stages.name: Resume at Selection Sunday: results, quality and strength
stages.description: Each team accumulates a resume over the season: the quality of wins and losses (quadrants determined by opponent rank and site), strength of schedule, wins above a bubble team and predictive efficiency. How the final resume looks depends on the remaining games, which differ in leverage: a win over a top-30 opponent on the road adds much more than a home win over a 250th-ranked team, while a loss to a Q3 or Q4 team costs heavily.
stages.distribution: Resume metrics are ordinal or bounded: quadrant counts are integers, WAB is approximately normal with sd of about 1 win by February, NET rank changes by 2 to 6 positions per game for bubble teams.

stages.name: Committee ranking as revealed preference with noise
stages.description: The committee does not apply a formula: it weighs NET, quadrant records, predictive metrics and its own judgement, and the weighting shifts between the top of the field, where quality wins and predictive rating matter more, and the bubble, where record against the quadrants dominates. A fitted ordered-probit on past seeds estimates the weights and the committee noise, which is of the order of two to four seed slots at the boundaries. Recent results may weigh more than early-season ones.
stages.distribution: Ordered-probit style latent score with committee noise sd about 2 to 4 rank slots; metric weights differ across seed ranges.

stages.name: Automatic bids and bid thieves
stages.description: Each of the roughly 30 conferences sends its tournament champion automatically. When a champion would not have been selected at-large (a bid thief), the number of at-large slots available to bubble teams falls by one. The count of thieves is random and depends on the conference tournaments of multi-bid leagues; a 3-bid league that loses its favourite in the tournament can produce a thief. This count shifts the cutoff by several slots.
stages.distribution: The number of bid thieves is approximately Poisson-binomial with mean 1 to 3 per year; each additional thief moves the effective at-large cutoff by one slot.

stages.name: Availability and committee treatment of injuries
stages.description: A team missing a key player at Selection Sunday may be seeded as a team that would play without him (committee principles mention availability) or as it was over the season, with unclear weighting. Because disclosure is thin, the market and the model may disagree on whether a star will be back, and an injury in the conference tournament changes the committee's view without changing any metric much.
stages.distribution: Binary-like treatment effect on seed with magnitude of 0 to 2 lines for key players out; uncertain sign convention across years.

stages.name: S-curve placement and bracketing constraints
stages.description: After ranking, teams are placed on the S-curve in seed lines of four, then adjusted to satisfy rules: no same-conference matchups before a stated round where avoidable, balanced regions, proximity placements for top seeds and pod site assignments. These adjustments can move a team one seed line away from its rank-implied line, and the effect is a discrete jump in seed distribution.
stages.distribution: Discrete seed-line assignment with a most likely value and neighbours at 15 to 30 percent probability each for teams near line boundaries.

stages.name: Advancement after seeding
stages.description: Once the bracket is set, round-reached outcomes are determined by single-game win probabilities along the path, with seed-specific historical base rates as a calibration target. A team's seed and region decide the opponents; upsets are driven by game variance and stylistic matchups. KXMARMADROUND pays on qualification for the named round, so for the first round it is a selection event, and for later rounds an advancement event. KXNCAAMBBOTHQUAL needs the joint advancement of two named teams, which is lowered (to zero if paired) when the bracket can bring them together before the Round of 16.
stages.distribution: Nested advancement events with monotone probabilities; round-reached distribution is convex in rating gap and path strength.

stages.name: Bracket-wide seed statistics: upset counts, seed sums and the biggest upset
stages.description: Five series settle on statistics of the whole bracket rather than on one team: how many #k seeds reach a round or win a first-round game, how many seed-based upsets occur in a round, the sum of the four semifinalists' seeds, and the largest seed gap any winner overcame; the title-only KXMARMADHIGHSEED (highest seed to reach a round) is a statistic of the same simulated brackets. Each is a function of the joint outcome of many games, computed per simulated tournament. Their distributions are discrete and depend on the actual seed-line strength gaps of that year's field (a year with weak #1 seeds has more upsets everywhere) and on bracket structure (two #1 seeds in one half cannot both reach the final).
stages.distribution: Discrete count and extreme-value statistics per simulated bracket: upset counts approximately Poisson-binomial across the round's games, seed sums lumpy over 4 to 40, max seed difference concentrated at 7 to 13 with heavy mass on 15 when a 16-over-1 or 15-over-2 occurs.

stages.name: Regular-season win totals and undefeated runs
stages.description: KXNCAAMBWINS, KXNCAAMBUNDEFEATED and KXNCAAMBUNDEFEATEDHOME count only official regular-season games. The win total is a sum of correlated game outcomes over roughly 30 games whose probabilities share one uncertain strength, so its distribution is wider than a fixed-probability Poisson-binomial; an unbeaten season is the extreme upper tail, dominated by the few road games against strong conference opponents. The home-only variant uses the 14 to 17 games in the team's own arena, where per-game win probabilities are higher, so it is far likelier than an unbeaten season but hinges on the strongest home conference visitors.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed Poisson-binomial over the counted games; P(undefeated) is an integral over the strength draw of a product of per-game probabilities, roughly exponential in strength.

availability_news.note: Committee treatment of injured stars and communications of status at Selection Sunday.

coaching_scheme.note: The relevant coaching-like layer is the committee's behaviour (chair, members, protocol), not team coaches.

environment.note: Home, away and neutral allocation decides the undefeated, home-undefeated and win-total series; neutral-site games are excluded from the home series.

game_context_script.note: In-game script has no role in committee selection other than through final scores in NET margin components (capped), which are already inside the resume metrics.

pace_volume.note: Possession counts are not a driver of selection or seed lines; tempo affects only game variance, which is addressed in advancement.

efficiency_conversion.note: Net efficiency is a component of NET and of the predictive ratings the committee consults.

distribution_variance.note: Seed distributions are ordinal with committee noise; advancement distributions nested.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Remaining schedule and tournament games as the way the resume changes before Selection Sunday.

officiating_rules.note: Game officiating is not an input to selection; the relevant rules are the committee's principles and procedures, covered under protocol and settlement inputs.

settlement_contract.note: Rules text read for 13 of 14 series (selection, seed lines, round qualification paying without competing, bracket-wide seed statistics, regular-season-only counts, home-arena-only games); HIGHSEED has no listing.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Fourteen series in three groups. Selection and seeding (settle on the committee's bracket): KXMARMAD1SEED (#1 seed), KXMARMADSEED (#1 or #2 seed), KXNCAAMBTEAMSQUAL (every listed team qualifies; one miss is NO), KXMARMADROUND (qualifies for a named round, sampled 'Round of 76'; YES even if the team does not compete). Tournament outcomes: KXNCAAMBBOTHQUAL (two named teams both reach the Round of 16), KXMARMADSEEDROUND (exact count of #k seeds reaching a round), KXMARMADSEEDWIN (count of #k seeds winning a game in a round), KXMARMADUPSET (count of upsets by seed in a round), KXMARMADSEEDSUM (sum of official seeds of the semifinalists in a range), KXMARMADSEEDDIF (largest seed margin overcome by any winner in the full tournament at least a strike), and title-only KXMARMADHIGHSEED. Regular season only: KXNCAAMBWINS (at least N regular-season wins), KXNCAAMBUNDEFEATED, KXNCAAMBUNDEFEATEDHOME (home games at the official home arena; neutral sites excluded).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: NCAA official selection bracket (NCAA.com) for seed and qualification series; the sampled rules name no source, and the title-only series may settle on tournament results.
variants_and_edge_cases: Seed-line contracts depend on the committee's S-curve and its bracketing constraints: a team ranked 8th among the top-seeded group can be moved a line to avoid same-conference matchups, so the seed line is not a deterministic function of rank.

Made-the-field contracts include automatic bids (conference tournament champions) and at-large bids; whether a team that qualifies but is later ineligible or withdraws counts is a settlement question (KXMARMADROUND in this archetype pays even if the team does not compete; TEAMSQUAL and the seed series state no such clause).

A play-in or First Four team and a 16 seed are both low seeds with different path lengths; if the 2027 field is expanded beyond 68 teams (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), the number of play-in games and which seeds play them changes round-reached definitions.

Round-reached contracts for a given round are nested events (reach round 2 includes reach round 3), so a ladder of strikes must have monotone probabilities and may be influenced by whether the play-in round counts as a round.

KXNCAAMBTEAMSQUAL lists teams of one conference (Duke, North Carolina, NC St.), whose selections are coupled through the conference's bid count and its tournament champion, so the joint probability exceeds the product of marginals when they share strength-of-schedule gains and is lower when they take wins from each other.

Bracket-count series (SEEDROUND, SEEDWIN, UPSET) are exact or at-least counts over the games of one round; SEEDSUM buckets the semifinalists' seed sum; SEEDDIF is a maximum over the full tournament, so whether First Four games count toward 'the full tournament' is not stated.

KXMARMADUPSET names the 'Round of 8' (Elite Eight) while other series use 'Round of 16'/'Round of 64'; round labels are Kalshi's, and the 'Round of 76' in KXMARMADROUND does not match a 68-team field.

Win totals and undefeated series count official regular-season games only; whether games against non-Division I opponents count, and the number of games a team plays (27 to 31), are not stated, and strikes such as 30 wins need near-perfection.
Undefeated at home excludes neutral-site games, conference-tournament and postseason games, so only 14 to 17 games in the team's own arena count.
KXNCAAMBBOTHQUAL is a joint advancement event that is zero if the two teams are drawn to meet before the Round of 16; same-conference avoidance rules reduce but do not remove that chance.

polls_and_awards.label: College basketball polls, #1 rank and awards
polls_and_awards.target: Which teams hold a poll rank or how many distinct teams hold #1, or an individual award winner.
polls_and_awards.mechanism: Poll position follows results, opponent rank and voter inertia; the number of distinct #1 teams is driven by upset probability among the top teams and voter reactions to losses. Player awards follow production, team success and narrative. Markets here are driven by schedule structure and voter behaviour, not game-level models alone.

inputs.why: Team strength for upset probability.
Voter inertia and reaction to losses decide how far a team falls after an upset, which determines whether #1 changes hands.
Resume metrics (quality wins, bad losses) are what voters reward beyond efficiency ratings.
Conference strength discounts or boosts a team's results in voters' eyes.
Remaining schedule decides loss risk.
Single-game upset variance by team style sets the per-game chance the top team loses.
Rating uncertainty widens the probability a ranked team is really weaker than its poll slot.
Production and usage form the statistical case for individual awards.
Injury and eligibility news can remove an award candidate or a top team without a game being played.
Defines the path-dependent count that the single-game upset variance input does not.
Allows a mechanical simulation of poll movement; the existing voter-behaviour input is a label without data or measurement.
Converts the bracket simulation into the final-rank distribution that two sampled series settle on.

Targets the specific computed object the series settle on rather than a generic rating ensemble. Not settlement-accurate: replication error of several tenths of a point decides near-tied ranks, so it is a calibration aid and the exact KenPom list is required for the final days (see pa_kenpom_replication).
Gives a candidate-level probability model per award type; the existing player_usage input is a statistic, not a selection process.
Derives the leader probability from the full structure instead of extrapolating the current top of the list.
Specifies the horizon and the labels the contracts use.
Primary team-strength term for the poll and KenPom contracts; fundamentals-only replacement of the market-contaminated cbb.ratings (benchmark-only).
Gives KXNCAAMBAWARD and KXNCAAMBCONFAWARD an actual selection model beyond news and usage; criteria differ by award type.
Required for KXNCAAMBCOTY, whose winner is driven by over-performance rather than strength.

interactions.hypothesis: Upset probability is rating gap scaled by team-style variance.
Voter reaction to a loss depends on opponent rank and timing.
Resume strength is discounted by weak conferences.

The drop in poll rank after a loss depends on who the opponent was and where the game was played: a road loss to a top-15 team moves a #1 team down a few places, while a home loss to an unranked team can drop it five or more; the same rating gap implies different poll movement depending on opponent rank and site.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress rank change after a loss on opponent AP rank, site, margin and prior rank using 10 seasons of AP polls and test the opponent-rank by site interaction.

interactions.hypothesis: The distinct-#1 count is far into the tail for strikes like 9, where the probability depends strongly and convexly on the per-week change probability: a rise in weekly change probability from 15 to 20 percent multiplies the probability of 9 or more holders several times because it requires many successive changes with new successors.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the Markov count under change probabilities from 10 to 25 percent and compare the implied P(>=9) to the empirical distribution of distinct #1 counts over 25 seasons.

interactions.hypothesis: The probability a named player wins Tournament MOP is the product of his team's probability of winning the title and his share of the vote within a champion; because the first factor is small for most teams (a fraction of a percent) and the second is concentrated in the top player, the product is extremely skewed toward stars on top seeds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predicted MOP probabilities from the product model against historical MOP team and player identities, including the non-champion exceptions.

interactions.hypothesis: A Final-poll top-10 or exact-rank outcome is decided mostly by the round a team reaches: within a round, pre-tournament AP rank orders teams, but a Final Four run lifts a team past almost any higher-ranked early loser, so the effect of pre-tournament rank on the final rank is large for early exits and small for deep runs.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit final AP rank on pre-tournament rank separately by round reached (2000-2026) and test whether the slope differs across rounds.

interactions.hypothesis: Each remaining poll is another chance for a never-before #1 team to take the top spot, but late in the season the pool of plausible new holders shrinks to teams already near the top, many of which have held #1 already, so additional polls add progressively fewer new distinct holders to the KXNCAAMBAPCHURN count.
interactions.how_to_test: Across past seasons, regress new-distinct-#1 events on poll index and the count of top-5 teams not yet #1; check that the per-poll hazard falls with the depleted pool.

interactions.hypothesis: The same 28-win season makes a strong coach-of-the-year case for a team picked to finish mid-conference but almost none for a preseason top-5 team, so the effect of team success on award probability is conditional on (and decreasing in) preseason expectation.
interactions.how_to_test: In past award voting, regress winner/finalist status on wins interacted with preseason AP rank and projected win%; expect a negative interaction.

nonlinearities.shape: asymmetric: rank loss after a defeat exceeds the rank gain after an equivalent win, and the drop is larger at the top of the poll
nonlinearities.why: Voters treat the #1 team's loss as more informative than a win and a #1 team that loses to an unranked opponent can fall many places, so rank movement is not linear in margin or rating gap and the top spot is fragile.

nonlinearities.shape: sigmoid in the rating gap to the next contender over projected rating sd for the weekly #1 hold
nonlinearities.why: Whether the current #1 keeps the top spot after a week depends on the gap to the next team relative to how much one or two results can move voters' view; small gaps make the hold probability fall steeply, large gaps make it nearly flat.

nonlinearities.shape: convex effect on tail counts of distinct #1 teams
nonlinearities.why: Because the probability of nine or more holders needs repeated losses with new successors, a small rise in single-game upset variance causes a disproportionately large rise in the tail probability.

mechanism_review.summary: Three different data-generating processes sit under this key. Poll series are a human aggregation of results: about 60 voters rank 25 teams each week, a team's rank moves with its results, the quality of opponent, and voter inertia, so the distinct-#1 count is a path-dependent Markov process in which each week the current #1 loses with a small probability and a successor is chosen from the contenders; the any-week top-5 series is a running minimum of rank and the Final-poll series are tournament-advancement contracts filtered through voters. Player award series are two-stage: team success (for Tournament MOP) or season production and narrative (for Naismith and conference awards) determines the candidate set, and a within-set selection picks the winner, with a split-payout rule and a No for a non-playing candidate where stated. The coach award is a vote on team over-performance relative to preseason expectation.

stages.name: Game results of top teams as the shock process
stages.description: Everything in the poll series is downstream of game results of the highest-ranked teams: the weekly chance that the #1 team loses is roughly one minus the win probability in about 1.5 games per week, higher in conference play against ranked teams and road games. A single-game loss probability of 8 to 15 percent for #1 means about one loss every 5 to 8 weeks, so over the roughly 19 polls several changes at #1 are plausible, and the count of distinct holders is a function of both loss frequency and who replaces the loser.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli loss events per week with probabilities from the rating gap and venue; rare but compounding over 19 polls; positively correlated across top teams through shared schedule strength.

stages.name: Voter aggregation and succession at the top
stages.description: Each weekly AP poll is the points total of about 60 individual ballots; voters update ballots after results with inertia (a team usually falls fewer places for a close loss to a strong opponent than for a loss to an unranked team) and some voters prefer unbeaten or recently strong teams. When #1 loses, the successor is typically the highest-ranked team that has not lost recently, but the poll often elevates a new team rather than a previously ranked #1, which is what adds to the distinct count. The per-voter ballots are published by the AP, which enables a voter-level model.
stages.distribution: Aggregate points are a sum of voter-specific ranks with positive correlation between voters; probability that a given team becomes the new #1 follows a softmax over contenders by recent results, rating and prior rank.

stages.name: Final poll after the tournament
stages.description: The Final Rankings are published after the title game and mainly reorder teams by tournament outcome: the champion is typically first or close to it, the runner-up and Final Four teams follow, early exits drop, and teams that missed the tournament fall further. A rank threshold such as top 10 is therefore an advancement contract (reaching the Elite Eight or Final Four) layered on pre-tournament rank, and a specific position such as #3 depends on the order among Final Four teams.
stages.distribution: Rank is an ordinal function of round reached and pre-tournament rank with noise of about 1 to 2 places; probability of a given rank is bell-shaped around the expected rank.

stages.name: Player awards: selection of a winner from a candidate set
stages.description: For the NCAA Tournament Most Outstanding Player (KXNCAAMBAWARD, KXNCAAMBMOP) the candidate set is the Final Four and the winner is nearly always from the champion, so probability is the team's title probability times the player's selection share on that team (driven by scoring in the Final Four games and star status). For Naismith Player of the Year the candidates are national stars and voters weigh season production, team record and narrative, with the field narrowing through watch lists and finalists. For conference awards such as Defensive Player of the Year the candidate set is the conference's players. Co-winners split payout where the text says so.
stages.distribution: Multinomial selection with strong dependence on team success; within the champion, selection share is concentrated (the top player typically holds 40 to 70 percent); co-recipient probability is small but nonzero.

stages.name: Coach of the Year: over-performance against preseason expectation
stages.description: KXNCAAMBCOTY settles on the Naismith Coach of the Year vote. Voters reward a coach whose team far exceeds preseason expectation (record and ranking well above preseason poll and projections), wins a major conference or makes a deep tournament run, and first-year turnarounds; coaches of perennial favourites rarely win for merely meeting expectations. The candidate pool therefore depends on in-season results relative to the preseason baseline, and late-season results before the vote dominate.
stages.distribution: Categorical winner over roughly 10 to 20 plausible coaches; heavily skewed toward two or three over-performers by March, with a long tail early in the season.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Nine series. AP poll series settle only on the AP Top 25 on the Associated Press website: the number of distinct teams ranked #1 across all polls including Preseason and Final (KXNCAAMBAPCHURN), a team's exact rank (KXNCAAMBAPRANK) or top-10 status (KXNCAAMBTOPAPRANK) in the Final Rankings expected Apr 6, 2027, or a top-5 rank in any eligible poll (KXNCAAMBAPANY). Award series settle on the named winner: NCAA Tournament Most Outstanding Player (KXNCAAMBAWARD, KXNCAAMBMOP), conference awards (KXNCAAMBCONFAWARD), Naismith Player of the Year (KXNCAAMBNAISMITH) and Naismith Coach of the Year (KXNCAAMBCOTY). AWARD and CONFAWARD pay Yes $1/N (rounded down to the cent) to N co-recipients and resolve No for a player who does not play in the season; the MOP, Naismith and COTY texts state neither rule.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: AP Top 25 on the official Associated Press website for poll series; official award announcements (NCAA for Tournament MOP, the Naismith Awards for Player and Coach of the Year, conferences for conference awards) for honours; the award texts name no source.
variants_and_edge_cases: Poll churn counts every poll in the season (Preseason through Final), so the number of polls (about 19 to 20) is the number of opportunities for a new #1; a team that is #1 in the preseason counts as soon as the first poll is released.
KXNCAAMBAPANY (any week, top 5) can resolve YES immediately on the Preseason poll or any weekly poll and cannot revert; it is a running-minimum of rank, with a Final poll as the last opportunity.

Final-ranking series (APRANK, TOPAPRANK) depend on tournament results because the Final poll is released after the title game (expected Apr 6, 2027); the champion is typically voted first or near first, so these are advancement contracts in disguise.

Award contracts: KXNCAAMBAWARD and KXNCAAMBCONFAWARD resolve No for a player who does not play in the season and pay Yes $1/N rounded down to the cent (No $1 minus that) to N co-recipients; NCAA Tournament Most Outstanding Player is almost always from the champion, so it is a title contract multiplied by a within-team selection.
Tournament MOP is listed twice (KXNCAAMBAWARD sampled as Tournament MOP, and KXNCAAMBMOP) with different texts: only AWARD states the 1/N co-recipient and non-play rules.

Naismith Player and Coach of the Year are national votes announced around the Final Four; the texts name only the winner, so co-winners, a player who leaves mid-season and announcement timing are not addressed.

kenpom_rating_snapshot.label: KenPom rating rank snapshot
contract_types: Men's College Basketball KenPom Top Ratings
kenpom_rating_snapshot.target: Team's rank on the KenPom ratings at a fixed timestamp (exact rank or top-N)
kenpom_rating_snapshot.mechanism: The outcome is the position of a team in a deterministic efficiency-margin list recomputed from all D1 results, read at Mar 15, 2027 12:00pm EST (the Monday after Selection Sunday, with no D1 games scheduled that day). From a November pricing date the horizon is the whole season: the preseason prior is phased out, true strength drifts with roster integration and injuries, and some 28-34 games each move AdjEM by an opponent-adjusted surprise. By March only 0-4 games remain. The probability is an order-statistic crossing problem set by AdjEM gaps, remaining rating variance, update sensitivity and which results the Monday-noon page has processed.

inputs.why: Direct replication and forward projection of the KenPom list to the snapshot time; the contract is literally a rank in that list.
Stored daily snapshots give the starting ranks and the realised daily rank volatility without retroactive revision.
Rank is an order statistic, so the AdjEM gap to the neighbouring ranks at the cutoff decides how easily results flip it.
Converts each remaining game's margin and opponent into an AdjEM change, the only way a rank can move.
Fixes which results the Monday-noon page contains: Selection Sunday finals and the overnight refresh, the EST/EDT label and downtime.
Offensive component of the rating being ranked; needed to replicate AdjEM and to project future game efficiency.
Defensive component of the rating being ranked; needed to replicate AdjEM and project future game efficiency.
Margin per possession is scaled by possessions, and tempo shifts how far one game moves AdjEM.
Fundamentals-only ensemble supplies win probabilities and margins for the remaining games without betting lines.
Byes, bracket size and neutral sites fix how many games each team plays before the snapshot.
Blowout versus competitive regimes determine how margins translate into the efficiency the algorithm sees.
Late-season absences change expected efficiency in the final games before the snapshot.
Posterior sd of each team's rating and the residual preseason-prior weight set how far a rank can move from November to March.
Versioned wording fixes the ratings page, timestamp and what Yes means.
Settled value and time show which page state the exchange actually read.
Season-horizon variance of AdjEM from the pricing date to Mar 15, combining prior phase-out and true-strength drift; dominant from November to January.
KenPom starts from a preseason prior that is phased out over the season, so the prior's error is a main source of early rank movement.
Returning minutes and transfer integration predict how far a team's true strength departs from its preseason rating as the season develops.
Player impact values convert portal arrivals, freshmen and injuries into expected efficiency changes over the remaining season.
Remaining schedule strength and venue mix set expected margins and how much opponent re-adjustment the team will see before Mar 15.
Conference seeding and tiebreakers decide byes and so the number of conference-tournament games before the snapshot.
Availability-adjusted strength for the active set gives expected game efficiency when a key player is out before the snapshot.
Own and opponent three-point luck in realised efficiency tends to regress, giving an expected direction of AdjEM drift.
Home, away and neutral coding sets the venue adjustment of each game margin entering the rating.
Conference tournaments and early-season events are at neutral or semi-home sites, which changes the venue term of those games.

interactions.hypothesis: A flip needs the per-game update to be large relative to the AdjEM gap, so the same remaining schedule is safe for a team with a wide gap and live for a bunched one.

Extra tournament games add variance to a high-rated team's rank because the rating only falls if it under-performs its expected margin, and bye teams carry less variance than teams that must play three games.
Blowout margins earn diminishing rating credit, so heavy favourites gain little from beating weak conference-tournament opponents while narrow wins can still cost rating.
Rank volatility from November to January is largest for high-churn rosters, because the phased-out prior was least informative for them and true strength moves most.

A rank flips only when the cumulative AdjEM move of the team and its neighbours exceeds the local gap. The probability behaves like a normal-tail crossing in the ratio of gap to per-game update sd times root games left, so risk is low until the ratio falls below about 1.
interactions.how_to_test: Build z = gap / (sd_game * sqrt(games_left)) per team-day and check that realised flip frequency over prior seasons is a steep logistic in z, with a clear knee near z of 1.

interactions.hypothesis: A first-round bye removes one or two games, so a bye team's rank variance is smaller; a top seed that is knocked out early loses little rating if it still performed close to expectation, whereas deep runs add variance in both directions.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare day-to-day rank change sd over Mar 8-15 between bye and non-bye top-40 teams in past seasons, conditioning on games played in the window.

interactions.hypothesis: Because large margins are discounted by the algorithm, a high-offence team that wins by 30 gains much less than 3 times the credit of a 10-point win, so projected AdjEM gains from soft opponents are muted and a close win can reduce AdjEM.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress next-day dAdjEM on margin versus expected margin with a spline; the slope should flatten beyond about 15 to 20 points above expectation.

interactions.hypothesis: A key player's absence lowers true strength immediately, but the rating reflects it only after games are played without him, so a team's rank on Mar 15 can lag its true strength; the lag matters in bunched regions.
interactions.how_to_test: Event study of teams losing a top-two impact player in the last three weeks: compare AdjEM change over the next 10 days to the lineup-adjusted rating drop.

interactions.hypothesis: Only teams that played a Selection Sunday final can be affected by a delayed overnight refresh or downtime, and only if they sit within a few tenths of a cutoff; the two conditions must hold together, so the risk is a small joint tail.
interactions.how_to_test: In past seasons flag teams that played on Selection Sunday, compare their Monday 12:00 ET rank with the rank after the last Sunday result was processed, and split by gap bucket.

interactions.hypothesis: The variance of AdjEM to Mar 15 depends on the residual weight of the prior: in November a high-churn team's rating can move several points and flip a top-25 position, while by February the same roster churn adds little because results dominate.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress |AdjEM change to Mar 15| on returning-minutes share interacted with pricing month over 5 past seasons; the churn slope should fall sharply after January.

nonlinearities.shape: step-like: flip probability near zero until gap falls below about one per-game update sd
nonlinearities.why: Rank changes need an actual crossing of neighbouring AdjEM values, so risk is a sharply nonlinear function of gap and clusters of teams within half a point multiply it.

nonlinearities.shape: assumed hyperbolic decay in games played (about 1/g), pending calibration under kp_algo
nonlinearities.why: Each game should carry less weight as the season lengthens, so a mid-March blowout moves AdjEM much less than a November one; the exact form is not published and must be fitted.

nonlinearities.shape: concave in points margin beyond expectation
nonlinearities.why: The algorithm discounts garbage-time and very large margins, so rating credit saturates while the downside for a poor performance does not.

nonlinearities.shape: remaining sd concave in days to snapshot, reaching zero at Mar 15
nonlinearities.why: Prior phase-out and drift accumulate quickly early and slowly later, so remaining rating variance falls steeply after January and rank prices should firm.

mechanism_review.summary: The outcome is a rank in an algorithmic list, not a vote. KenPom ranks all D1 teams by adjusted efficiency margin, an opponent- and venue-adjusted points-per-100-possessions margin computed from every game so far and, early in the season, blended with a preseason prior that is phased out. Markets list in November, so a rank on Mar 15, 2027 is (1) the current rating state, plus (2) season-horizon change: the prior's error being revealed, true-strength drift from roster integration, injuries and shooting-luck regression, which dominate from November to January, plus (3) the games still to play, about 28-34 in November and 0-4 in March, including conference-tournament survival, plus (4) the update each result causes, large early and small late, rewarding beating the expected margin rather than winning, and moving neighbours too through opponent re-adjustment, plus (5) the order-statistic mapping from AdjEM values to a rank, where local density at the cutoff sets fragility, and (6) the page state at Monday noon after Selection Sunday. The #1 contract is a single-slot race between a few teams; top-25 is a boundary-crossing problem against a bunched cluster.

stages.name: Starting rating state
stages.description: The KenPom list at pricing time is a deterministic function of every D1 result so far plus, early in the season, the preseason rating: per-team adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency per 100 possessions, tempo, and opponent adjustment solved jointly across the connected schedule. The starting rank, the AdjEM level and the gap to neighbouring ranks are observable from the ratings table or approximated by Torvik's T-Rank. In November the list is mostly prior; by March it is almost entirely results.
stages.distribution: Near-continuous AdjEM values; the rank is a discrete order statistic with local density that is high around #25 and thin at the top.

stages.name: Prior phase-out and true-strength drift
stages.description: From a November pricing date the dominant uncertainty is not the next game but how far each team's rating will travel by mid-March. The preseason prior, built from returning minutes, transfers, recruiting and last season, is phased out, so its error is revealed game by game; true strength also drifts as portal players and freshmen integrate, injuries accumulate and lucky or unlucky three-point shooting regresses. High-churn rosters and teams with few connected games move most.
stages.distribution: AdjEM change from November to Mar 15 is roughly normal with sd of several points for high-churn teams and smaller for continuity teams; sd shrinks toward zero as the date approaches.

stages.name: Games still to be played
stages.description: Between pricing and Selection Sunday each team plays the rest of its schedule: from November about 28-34 games including nonconference events, conference play and the conference tournament; by March only the finale and 0-4 tournament games remain, set by format, byes, seed and elimination. Each game's margin comes from the matchup of strengths, venue and who is available, with single-game noise of about 10 points.
stages.distribution: Games remaining fall from about 30 in November to a small integer (0 to 4) in March with dependence on bracket survival; per-game margin is roughly normal with sd near 10 to 11 points and fatter blowout tails.

stages.name: Result to rating update
stages.description: Each completed game feeds the algorithm as an adjusted efficiency margin: points per 100 possessions relative to what the opponent usually allows, adjusted for venue, blended into the running rating with a weight that falls as games accumulate (assumed about one over games played; see kp_algo). Opponents are re-adjusted too, so a team's rank moves on days it does not play. Blowout margins appear to earn diminishing credit, so a close win over a weak team can lower the rating.
stages.distribution: Per-game rating change is mean-near-zero with sd of about a point in November and a few tenths of AdjEM in March; the sign depends on beating the expected margin rather than winning, giving a concave response to margin.

stages.name: Rank as an order statistic
stages.description: The settled quantity is the position of one team among about 360 AdjEM values after all updates. For an exact-rank contract the team must hold one specific position, so both its own movement and the movement of every neighbour matter and the probability is a thin slice. For top-25 the team must sit above the AdjEM of the 25th-26th boundary, so a bunched cluster makes flips likely. Ties in displayed rating are unlikely at two decimals but possible in rank ordering rules unknown to us.
stages.distribution: Probability mass is concentrated within a few ranks of the current position; exact-rank markets are far more concentrated and discrete than threshold markets, which behave like normal-tail crossing probabilities.

stages.name: Snapshot reading and settlement
stages.description: Resolution reads the ratings page at 12:00pm EST on Monday Mar 15, 2027 and nothing else. No games are played that day, so the risk is whether Sunday's late conference finals were processed in the overnight refresh, the EST versus daylight-time label, site downtime and any methodology change. There is no formal feed; the settlement source is whatever the page shows at that instant.
stages.distribution: Mostly deterministic once the page is read, but with a small probability of timing or refresh mismatches that flip teams sitting at a boundary.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Yes settles if the named team holds exactly the rank in the ticker (rank 1 sampled, KXNCAAMBKENPOMRANK) or is ranked 25 or better (KXNCAAMBKENPOMTOP) on the 2027 Pomeroy College Basketball Ratings as shown on Mar 15, 2027 at 12:00pm EST; resolution rests solely on that KenPom page at that instant. No D1 games fall on that Monday, so the counted results are those the page had processed after Selection Sunday; no fallback for downtime or ties is stated.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: KenPom (kenpom.com) Pomeroy College Basketball Ratings page read at Mar 15, 2027 12:00pm EST; single-operator site with no public API. The main ratings table is believed to be free to view while team pages and the dated ratings archive need a subscription; access tiers are not verified here (kp_source_access).
variants_and_edge_cases: Exact-rank markets (#1 sampled; other rank values may exist in the series) resolve on one slot, while top-25 is a threshold; the same team can be close to one and far from the other.
The label 12:00pm EST falls the day after US daylight time begins (Mar 14, 2027); whether it means 12:00 fixed-offset EST (13:00 EDT) or New York clock time is not stated in the sampled rules.
Rules do not say what happens if the site is unavailable at the timestamp, if the ranking is mid-refresh, or how tied ranks are shown; the sample is silent.

Mar 15, 2027 is the Monday after Selection Sunday (Mar 14) and before the Opening Round (Mar 16), so no D1 games are played on the snapshot day; the timing risk is whether Sunday's late conference finals were processed by the overnight refresh.
Season label '2027' ratings refer to the 2026-27 season; markets are listed in November 2026, so most of a contract's life has a full-season horizon rather than a final-week horizon.

race_to_n_points.label: CBB race to N points
contract_types: Men's College Basketball Race to Points
Men's College Basketball Race to 10 Points
Men's College Basketball Race to 25 Points
Men's College Basketball Race to 50 Points
race_to_n_points.target: Which team first reaches N points in a game (first-passage event)
race_to_n_points.mechanism: Each team's points arrive in discrete possession-by-possession chunks, so the race is a first-passage problem on two alternating scoring processes. The edge comes from the opening five's points per possession (prior-heavy and uncertain early in the season), the jump-ball winner's tie-break, early turnovers and rebounds, the bench units for N=50, and N itself: races to 10 are mostly variance, races to 50 approach the share of points over about 26 minutes. If markets trade in-play, the live score gap to N and possession dominate.

inputs.why: Team opening-segment scoring profile and opening-possession edge, the closest direct predictor of a first-passage race.
First-passage simulation on alternating possessions with tip-win edge, specific to a first-to-N contract.
Scales the edge by N because races to 10, 25 and 50 weigh luck and rating differently.
Opponent-adjusted offence sets points per possession for the team's unit in the race.
Opponent-adjusted defence sets the points per possession the rival unit concedes in the race.
Opening five and their health decide who is on the floor in the race segment before substitutions.
Late scratches change the starting lineup and thus scoring rate in the opening minutes.
Starter-unit on-floor efficiency is the actual scoring rate in the race window.
Possessions per minute fix how fast the points accumulate and how many tries each side gets.
Early-game pace relative to full game captures slow starts or quick openings by team.
Early three-point reliance drives a scoring distribution with lumpy 3-point jumps and fat tails.
Home court shapes opening-segment scoring through crowd and shooting familiarity.
Bonus and foul counts matter for the race to 50 where free throws may arrive before halftime.
Play-by-play ordering errors can flip close races and settlement lag affects resolution.
Wording defines the first to score N, game original date and postponement window.
Postponement and 48-hour rule decide whether a market resolves or goes to fair price.
Early-season efficiencies are mostly preseason prior, so the uncertainty of the rating gap dilutes its weight in the 25 and 50 races.
Markets list from early November, when the opening-unit scoring rate must be read off the preseason prior and roster churn.
A race to 50 runs to about minute 27 and uses bench units, whose scoring rate differs from the starters'.
If the market trades after tip, the current score gap to N, possession and clock replace pregame inputs as the main predictor.

interactions.hypothesis: The opening-possession tie-break matters most when both starting units score at similar rates, and it fades when one unit's points per possession clearly exceeds the other's.
A starting-lineup change inside the race window moves the unit's scoring rate more than the season rating suggests, so lineup news interacts with unit efficiency.
The same offensive gap converts into a larger race advantage at N=50 than at N=10 because the signal accumulates linearly while noise grows with the square root of possessions.
Bench-unit scoring matters only for races long enough to outlast the starters' first stint, so its weight is near zero at N=10 and material at N=50.

With near-equal points per possession the team with the first possession wins ties in possession count and gains a few percentage points; when one unit's rate is clearly higher the tie-break matters less, so the opening-possession effect depends on the rate gap.
interactions.how_to_test: On historical play-by-play, split races to 10 by first possession and by absolute gap in opening-unit points per possession and compare win rates across gap bins.

interactions.hypothesis: If a regular starter is out, the opening unit is a different five with a different scoring rate and the effect is concentrated in the first segment before the usual rotation resumes; the season's team rating understates this for races to 10.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare race-to-10 win rates for teams with a changed starter against baseline, controlling for adjusted offence.

interactions.hypothesis: Signal grows with the number of possessions and noise with its square root, so the effect of the offensive rating gap on the race win probability scales with N; at 10 it is slight, at 50 close to the full-game effect.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit logit race win on offence gap by N with an interaction term and check the slope increases monotonically from N=10 to 50.

interactions.hypothesis: Three-point heavy teams produce lumpier scores, and in a fast game more of those attempts occur in the window, increasing the chance of an early 9-0 run and spreading the first-passage time distribution.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare variance of points after 6 possessions for high and low three-point rate teams, and condition on pace tercile.

interactions.hypothesis: Reaching 50 depends on whether bonus free throws begin before the team gets there; once a team enters the bonus the points per possession rises, which switches the late race regime for teams that foul early.
interactions.how_to_test: For N=50 races, compare crossing times for games where either team entered the bonus before 12:00 of the first half against games where neither did.

interactions.hypothesis: The rating gap should drive N=50 races more than N=10, but in November the gap is mostly prior and uncertain, so the slope on the gap at N=50 should be flatter early in the season and steepen after conference play begins.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit race-to-50 win on the pregame rating gap with an interaction by month of season; expect a smaller slope in November-December.

interactions.hypothesis: Bench units enter after the first media timeouts, so their scoring rate affects only races still open at that point; a weak bench costs a team the race to 50 but not the race to 10.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress race-to-50 outcome on starter-unit and bench-unit efficiency gaps separately, and compare with race-to-10 where the bench coefficient should be near zero.

nonlinearities.shape: increasing concave in N toward the full-game win probability
nonlinearities.why: Favourite's race probability rises with N because mean accumulates linearly and sd as a square root, but saturates near the pregame win probability.

nonlinearities.shape: tie-break edge decays with N and with offensive-rebound rate
nonlinearities.why: The first-possession edge exists only while strict alternation holds, and it is larger when jumpers are mismatched; the more possessions and extra offensive-rebound tries, the more it washes out.

nonlinearities.shape: convex tail in the probability of a 9-0 start
nonlinearities.why: Points come in lumps of 3, so a handful of threes quickly produces a fast opening run and the likelihood of a very early crossing grows convexly with 3-point reliance.

mechanism_review.summary: The outcome is which team's cumulative score hits N first, a first-passage event on two interleaved point-accumulation processes. Points come in discrete amounts (free throws, twos, threes) on possessions that alternate between the teams, so for small N the winner is largely determined by the unit that starts, the tip and opening possession, and a few variance-heavy possessions. As N rises, the rating gap in points per possession accumulates linearly while noise grows with the square root of possessions, so the race approaches the full-game share of scoring, and the identity of the unit shifts from starters to rotation. Team defence matters through the rival's rate, tempo through time but little through relative advantage, and bonus free throws and early fouls matter for the 50-point race. Early in the season the rating gap is itself uncertain, which dilutes its weight. If the market trades after tip, the live gap to N and possession dominate. Settlement follows the official scoring sequence; no ties are possible.

stages.name: Opening possession and tip
stages.description: The game begins with a jump ball and the winner takes the first possession. Because the teams alternate possessions, the team that starts with the ball is first whenever both need the same number of possessions to reach N. Tip-win probability is not a coin flip: jumper height and wingspan mismatch and each jumper's historical tip record move it well off 0.5, and the edge is largest in the race to 10. It is known only after tip.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli tip outcome with a pregame probability that can range well away from 0.5 for mismatched jumpers; converted into a few points of race probability that shrink as N grows from 10 to 50.

stages.name: Starting-unit scoring rate
stages.description: For the first four to ten minutes the players on the floor are the announced starters, so the relevant rate is the points per possession of that five against the opponent's opening five, not season-long team efficiency. In November that rate is mostly preseason prior after portal churn, so its uncertainty matters. Press, zone, rim protection and three-point reliance shift the rate, and a late injury changes the opening five.
stages.distribution: Points per possession per trial is discrete (0,1,2,3, sometimes 4) with mean near 1.0 and sd near 1.1, so total points after k possessions has heavy lumpiness; team rates differ by a few tenths of a point per possession.

stages.name: Possession count and continuation
stages.description: The number of possessions in the window depends on pace, the share of turnovers and offensive rebounds that break alternation and how quickly each team shoots. Tempo is shared, but a team that forces early turnovers or crashes the offensive glass gets more tries inside the same stretch of game clock. A slow team facing a fast one can still be pulled into the faster pace early.
stages.distribution: Possessions inside the race window are a small count (about 8 to 12 per team for N=10), nearly equal for both sides with a skew from offensive rebounds and steals.

stages.name: Threshold crossing by N
stages.description: The outcome is a first-passage time: the first team whose cumulative points reach N. A 10-point race ends within roughly the first five minutes and mostly reflects luck; a 25-point race ends near the 10th to 12th minute after first substitutions; a 50-point race often ends after halftime, around minute 27, so bench-unit scoring, foul trouble and second-half team-foul resets and bonus free throws matter for who gets there first.
stages.distribution: Crossing times are discrete with overshoot (a 3-pointer can jump from 8 to 11); variance of the points gap grows like sqrt of possessions, so the favourite's race probability rises with N toward the full-game win probability.

stages.name: Event sequencing and settlement
stages.description: Settlement depends on the order of scoring events. Points are scored one event at a time (free throws are sequential), so there are no simultaneous crossings and no ties; the residual risk is an official-scorer or play-by-play correction to the sequence. KXNCAAMBRACE adds a 48-hour postponement window then fair-price resolution; the FIRST series samples show no such clause, and no series states overtime or neither-reaches-N handling.
stages.distribution: Mostly deterministic once the scoring sequence is final; small probability of a sequence correction, of postponement-driven fair-price resolution, or of an unstated N=50 edge case.

stages.name: In-play state (only if the market trades after tip)
stages.description: If KXNCAAMBRACE stays open after tip, the race becomes a first-passage problem from the current state: points still needed by each team, who has possession, the clock, and which units are on the floor. The pregame inputs then matter only through the remaining scoring rates, and stale quotes after a scoring run are the main risk. Whether trading continues in play is not visible in the evidence.
stages.distribution: Conditional on the state, a short random walk in possessions to the remaining gap; probabilities jump on every score and change of possession.
